💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Celtic legend is a Celtic Season Ticket Alliance Trust ambassador and is back in Scotland from his base in Australia to launch his autobiography and raise awareness of Willie Haughey’s independent supporter initiative.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Paul McStay believes major shareholder Dermot Desmond is not planning to walk away “anytime soon” from Celtic as he underlined the importance of fans having a say in the running of the club.

The Celtic legend is a Celtic Season Ticket Alliance Trust ambassador and is back in Scotland from his base in Australia to launch his autobiography and raise awareness of Willie Haughey’s independent supporter initiative.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

According to McStay, almost 5,000 of Celtic’s 54,000 season ticket holders have joined to date amid continued civil unrest at the club.

McStay, who plans to attend Saturday’s home game against St Mirren, is a link between the board and fans and witnessed the discontent first hand when he was invited to Parkhead last season to unfurl the title flag.

He cites the spirit of the team that overcame Hearts on the final day of the league season in 1986, when he was in his pomp in midfield, as the inspiration behind the Alliance’s efforts to reach a long-term goal.

According to recent reports, “I go back to the ‘86 year, when we won the league,” he said. “Hearts were there dominant in pole position. If we wanted to have success and win that league as players and manager Davie Hay, we have to stay focused on what our objective was. It was win each game at a time. With the Alliance, our objective is 10,000 season ticket holders signed up and Willie Haughey states he will put money in and buy shares.

“I understand the frustrations last year, because of the European situation and Kairat,” he added. “The boycotts, the protests. I understand that. But I think there is a better way to move forward, a more professional, business-like way and try and get someone on the board to talk and communicate and provide sports opinion.”.

He revealed he has discussed these aims with under-fire chief executive Michael Nicholson at a recent match.

Recent findings suggest that “I go to games,” he mentioned. “Last year I was back and invited as a guest to raise the flag so I was here when all the protests and boycotts were happening. The Celtic supporters want the best for their club but it is slightly different to what I think should be done. Again, that is about opinions. Even a couple of weeks ago I was at a game and I bumped into Michael – I am quite happy to give my opinions, whether that is in the dressing room with fellow players at the time or as captain talking to Fergus (McCann) or Billy McNeill or Liam Brady.”.

Recent findings suggest that an agm is scheduled for the start of next month. Last year’s meeting had to be cut short after Ross Desmond, Dermot’s son, was harangued while reading a pre-prepared statement from his father, who is not expected to attend this year's meeting either.

“You ask about Dermot and his position there,” remarked McStay. “He has put shares in the club. But to me I don’t think he is going to go anywhere soon. To me, this is a long-term objective. It might take time but we have to focus on what we are doing and build up support within our organisation to build up equity to give Celtic supporters a voice on the board. I think that will help things.”.

When are the 2026-27 Nations League quarter-finals? Dates, fixtures, teams, how they qualified

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (541 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 11:54, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 11:57.
  • The 2026-27 UEFA Nations League quarter-finals will take place in March 2027.
  • The draw for the final eight will take place on November 20, 2026, where it will be decided which teams will face off against each other for a spot in the semi-finals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 11:54, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 11:57.

The 2026-27 UEFA Nations League quarter-finals will take place in March 2027.

The draw for the final eight will take place on November 20, 2026, where it will be decided which teams will face off against each other for a spot in the semi-finals.

Here, Sports Mole runs through all of the details surrounding next year's matches, including dates, fixtures and how each of the eight teams booked a spot in the quarter-finals.

The first legs of the respective last-eight contests will take place between March 25 and March 27, 2027, with the second legs occurring between March 28 and March 30, 2027.

The draw for the quarter-finals of the 2026-27 Nations League will take place at 11am UK time on November 20 at UEFA's headquarters.

Finishing first in the section means that home advantage is gained for the second leg, while the winners of each group will take on a runner-up from another section.

France, Germany, England and Portugal have been the group winners, with Belgium, Netherlands, Spain and Norway qualifying as runners-up in each section.

Portugal are the holders of the Nations League trophy and also the most successful side in the history of the competition, having won it twice (2019 and 2025).

Spain (2023) and France (2021) have also won the tournament.

Germany, England, Belgium, Netherlands and Norway could become first-time winners of the Nations League in 2026-27, with the final set to take place in June 2027.

France finished first in Group A1 to secure a spot in the quarter-finals of the tournament, claiming 13 points from their six matches, boasting a record of four wins, one draw and one defeat.

Belgium were second in Group A2, one point behind the section winners France, having claimed 12 points from their six games, boasting a record of four wins and two defeats from six games.

Germany finished at the top of Group A2 with 11 points from six matches. Incredibly, each of Germany, Netherlands and Greece had 11 points from six games, but Germany finished at the summit on UEFA''s head-to-head goal difference tiebreaker.

Netherlands managed to sneak second spot in Group A2 ahead of Greece on overall goal difference, with Xavi's team finishing with a record of three wins, two draws and one defeat from six matches.

England spectacularly secured first position in Group A3 courtesy of their standout 3-2 success over Spain in Madrid on Sunday night; the Three Lions won five and lost one of their six games to collect 15 points, and they ultimately had a better overall goal difference.

Spain were bumped back down to second spot in Group A3 due to their loss to England; the reverse to the Three Lions proved to be their first defeat in 90 minutes since March 2024.

Portugal finished at the top of Group A4, boasting 15 points from their six matches, in order to comfortably secure a position in the quarter-finals of the tournament.

Norway managed to sneak into second spot in Group A4 ahead of Denmark on the final matchday, recording a 3-2 success over the Danes, which gave them the advance in the head-to-head tiebreaker.

Scottish football history made as youngest ever manager appointed - ‘I know there will be criticism’

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (643 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Scotsman

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Dumbarton have made history by appointing the youngest manager in the history of the SPFL.
  • Martin Fellowes has been installed as the new head coach of the League Two side at the age of 28.
  • Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dumbarton have made history by appointing the youngest manager in the history of the SPFL.

Martin Fellowes has been installed as the new head coach of the League Two side at the age of 28.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He leaves his position as assistant manager and head of football operations at league leaders Stranraer to join a team six places further down the table.

Fellows spent almost 10 years with East Kilbride, were he started as a teenage kit boy, working his way up to interim manager in 2023, and winning the Lowland League Cup during a two-month spell in charge.

He has a day job in office furniture sales and holds a Uefa A licence.

Industry observers note that "You have to earn people's respect as a person," Fellowes told BBC Scotland. "When you are a young guy and you're leading a football club, I don't think you can come in and change everything and lead with an iron fist.

Industry observers note that "You have to get people's respect on and off the pitch. I know there will be plenty of criticism and there will be plenty of people sitting here today doubting that I'm capable of doing this job at 28.

"But now really the work for me has started on, by the end of the process, having gained those people onside to say, 'he was more than capable of doing this job and we're delighted to have him here'.

"I can only do that through winning games of football.".

Fellowes claims the mantle of Scottish football’s youngest ever head coach from Jim Duffy, who was 29 when he took charge of Falkirk in 1988, while Rhys McCabe was appointed player/manager of Airdrieonians at the same age four years ago.

Former St Mirren and Clyde manager Danny Lennon, now Dumbarton director of football, revealed age was not a factor when considering who to appoint as a replacement for Frank McKeown, who was sacked last month.

“What really impressed us about Martin was his football knowledge, the clarity of his coaching philosophy, his understanding of player development and the passion and ambition he has for the game,” Lennon stated.

“Throughout our conversations, Martin demonstrated a real understanding of how he wants his teams to play, the standards he expects and how he intends to help players improve, both individually and collectively.

“He is a young and ambitious coach who has worked extremely hard to develop his knowledge and prepare himself for an opportunity as a head coach in the SPFL. I believe football should always be about recognising ability and potential, regardless of age or background.

Sources indicate that “Martin has earned this opportunity through the commitment he’s shown to his development and the qualities he’s demonstrated throughout the recruitment process. We fully appreciate that managing at this level comes with challenges, and it’s vital that we provide him with the right environment and support to succeed.

“We have a group of players who have shown a genuine willingness to learn and improve, and we’re excited about the opportunity to continue that development under Martin’s leadership.

“Our ambitions remain clear. We want to improve performances, compete towards the top end of the league and establish a strong football identity that our supporters can be proud of.

Sources indicate that “This appointment is about both the present and the future of Dumbarton Football Club. We’re looking forward to working closely with Martin, supporting his development as a manager and, most importantly, helping him bring success to the club.

“I’d ask our supporters to get right behind Martin and the team as we begin this next chapter together.”.

Nelson Dida believes that Ruben Amorim is showing he is a ‘great’ coach, and he gave his take on the Endrick to AC Milan rumours.

If anyone knows about the pressure of playing for Milan, it is Dida. Having been at the club from 2000 to 2010, he made over 300 official appearances for the Rossoneri and was part of an era that brought in eight major trophies under Carlo Ancelotti.

It has been revealed that he is widely regarded as one of the finest goalkeepers of his generation and was decisive in the 2003 Champions League final penalty shootout against Juventus. He also returned briefly as a goalkeeping coach, working for a year with Maignan.

Dida spoke to reporters who were present at the Galbiati Trophy and he answered a few questions regarding his former team, with his words relayed by MilanNews.

How do you think Amorim is doing?

“Amorim is proving to be a great coach. He took over Milan and is having a fantastic season. I think the attention is right because at Milan you can never make mistakes, but he has the ability to keep the team together to do well in the league.”.

If Maignan is hurt, would you come back and put the gloves on?

Sources indicate that “We already have a goalkeeper at AC Milan: Lorenzo Torriani, a guy who’s doing well. I like him. Last year, too, he did well when he had opportunities. I think he’s a focused guy, if he gets more opportunities, he can continue to grow.”.

Are Milan growing towards something?

It has been revealed that “Milan are slowly growing. They’re doing well in the league, I think we can still do more, while in Europe we’re still missing something.”.

Would Endrick be a good signing?

Industry observers note that “Endrick is a great player for me. When I see him play, he looks a bit like Romario, who is a bit small, but when he’s in the penalty area, he’s decisive. When he’s had the opportunity to play, he’s also scored goals.

According to recent reports, “I think he can really do well for Real Madrid and the national team, but I don’t know if he’s available to join Milan. I hope a Brazilian returns to play in the Italian league soon and wears the Milan shirt.”.

#37544. Paul McStay on refusing Celtic autobiography request and saying ‘polite no thanks’ to Rangers

Paul McStay on refusing Celtic autobiography request and saying ‘polite no thanks’ to Rangers

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1388 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Scotsman

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that he was an elegant presence in the centre of the Parkhead side’s midfield for almost all the 1980s and a good chunk of the 1990s, albeit injury dogged him in the later stages of his magnificent one-club career.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Paul McStay paradox has been a feature of Scottish football for many years. Although his name continues to be sung at nearly every Celtic game, the man himself has been one of the least visible former players of the modern era.

It has been revealed that he was an elegant presence in the centre of the Parkhead side’s midfield for almost all the 1980s and a good chunk of the 1990s, albeit injury dogged him in the later stages of his magnificent one-club career. A clip of a podcast he recorded with former teammate Brian McClair recently caught the eye, as it also featured a remarkably well-preserved copy of an old Edinburgh-based music newspaper called Cut.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

An equally well preserved McStay, now 62, and McClair discussed featuring on the wrap around front cover of the February 1987 edition. Pat Nevin was not the only thinking man’s footballer at the time. Now based in Australia, which might account for McStay’s healthy radiance as well as the infrequent appearances, all of this must feel like another lifetime ago.

So why has it taken him so long to publish his memoirs? That is itself a long story and is one of the reasons why McStay, whose family has playing ties to Celtic dating back to the 1920s, is launching his long-awaited autobiography at the home of …….Queen’s Park Football Club.

Recent findings suggest that it was originally meant to be launched at the slightly more appropriate Celtic Park last year, while on a trip home to raise the title flag before the opening league game against St Mirren. “It didn’t work out that way,” he explains. “Basically the club sent an agreement for them to sign off on the book.”.

Celtic were unhappy with some parts, probably related to the vexed matter of his eventual exit in 1997 after 16 years of stellar, some might even say genius, service.

Sources indicate that the upshot is McStay has published his own book on his own terms. “I’m doing it independently, doing it on my own,” he says. “And I have been quite honest. It’s my book, my story, my life. So I just mentioned I couldn’t sign the agreement. I’ll do my own thing.”.

It has been revealed that if the club’s mantra is let the people sing then surely allowing former players, especially such loyal servants as McStay, to tell their own story should be taken as read. “I just thought: No, I can’t have that,” he says.

McStay was sent off just once (at Dens Park in a 1994 League Cup tie v Dundee) and was described by Alex Ferguson, after his testimonial against Manchester United in 1995, as the “ultimate professional”. He was also awarded an MBE by the Queen and picked it up from Her Majesty herself in 1997 at Holyrood Palace. Happily married to Ann Marie, with whom he has six children, he is one of the most uncontroversial players ever to play the game. He nevertheless makes for ravishingly good copy.

“I’ve just got to tell my story,” McStay indicates. “If people are not aware of that, that's why I'm happy to share it. I just felt it was time to put how I lived it and my perception about certain things that happened as well, and put it in black and white.”.

According to recent reports, one regrettable consequence of the delay in his story getting out there is that we have been denied knowledge of a transfer tale to end nearly all transfer tales. Never mind music magazines, McStay would have featured on the front page of every newspaper in the land if the then Celtic skipper had joined Rangers in 1992.

Industry observers note that the Ibrox club were buying nearly everyone else, including Mo Johnston in 1989, during this era, so why not make a play for the best player at their biggest rivals? The religion thing had already been put to bed with Johnston…..ahem. Manager Walter Smith made the cheeky enquiry through a mutual contact.

“That was a question put to me in ’92, yes,” confirms McStay, who includes this startling snippet in Maestro: The Paul McStay Autobiography. “It was a polite ‘no thanks’. I think that’s the best way of putting it.”.

In a recent development, he is sworn to secrecy on the identity of who was sent by Smith to sound him out. “I can't say,” he claims. “But I know he's a friend of Walter. I never spoke to Walter about it.” His relationship with the Rangers legend dated back to their involvement in Scotland youth teams, Smith as the budding coach and McStay one of the country’s brightest young hopes. “When you talk about mentors and things like that, Walter was up there,” he says. “Andy Roxburgh was youth team manager in ’82 when we won the Euros and Walter was part of that. Since then, there’s always been a bond. He is a wonderful man and obviously, he did well at Rangers, which had an effect on me. But as a person, I got on really well with Walter.”.

It has been revealed that the phrase ‘had an effect on me’ is a wonderful way of saying McStay, towards the end of his Celtic career, seemed perpetually pitted in an almost one-man battle to stop Rangers winning nine-in-a-row. It was unfair to him, just as the financial imbalance - McStay has a few things to say about Rangers' spending power in his book - was unfair for the rest of Scottish football.

Recent findings suggest that aberdeen rather than Celtic came closest to stopping the Ibrox side’s march. McStay endured six trophyless years between 1989 and an emotional Scottish Cup win under Tommy Burns in 1995.

Not long afterwards, reeling from an X-ray report confirming the “virtual obliteration” of part of his ankle joint, McStay accepted that he had to consider retirement. But intense rehabilitation work saw him make another return, although he was clearly toiling. He finally called it a day at the end of the 1996-97 season. The then owner Fergus McCann, along with others, helped make this already difficult decision a horrendous experience. He was given the feeling that Celtic thought he was “bluffing” about the injury in a bid to negotiate a fresh deal with another club.

It has been revealed that “The exit wasn't great,” he indicates, understating things hugely. "I never ever thought I'd leave Celtic in that way. There were a lot of good times along the way, as well as ups and downs….

In a recent development, "But to me, it was very crucial to get that message out about how it ended. Because even at that time, there was a bit of PR coming out about certain things. And it wasn't quite accurate. I don't know what the club will feel about that. But I've got to tell the story the way it happened. And that's it.”.

Encouraged by Tommy Burns, he gained his coaching certificates and applied for the Under-16 Academy coach’s position at Celtic during Martin O’Neill’s first stint in charge. However, former teammate Jim McInally got the job instead. Australia beckoned in 2010.

“I do enjoy the element of being able to hide away, out of the road,” he indicates. It must have been comforting to know that across the other side of the world, every time Celtic played, his name was being sung in the chorus of the stirring “Willie Maley” song, which will be familiar to nearly everyone who watches football in Scotland: “And they gave us James McGrory and Paul McStay….” It’s a paean to storied past, one McStay is an integral part of.

In a recent development, “That started when I stopped playing,” he indicates. “James McStay was actually in the original song and then, through time, the younger generations changed it to Paul.” Every day’s a school day in the manufacturer of a Maestro.

Paul McStay was speaking at the launch of his autobiography Maestro. To purchase copies of the Celtic legend's book go to paulmcstay.com.

  • Athletic Bilbao will be bidding to continue their strong run of form when they resume their La Liga campaign at home to Espanyol on Friday night.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 11:58, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 11:33.

Athletic Bilbao will be bidding to continue their strong run of form when they resume their La Liga campaign at home to Espanyol on Friday night.

The Lions have won three and drawn one of their last four matches in all competitions, while Espanyol have managed to pick up four points from their last two La Liga fixtures.

Athletic have a record of four wins, four draws and three defeats from their 11 league matches this season, with 16 points leaving them in seventh spot in the La Liga table.

The Basque outfit entered the international break off the back of a 1-1 draw with Osasuna, but they have managed to pick up seven points from their last three fixtures.

Edin Terzic's side also managed to progress in the Copa del Rey with a 6-1 win over Prat at the end of October, so it has been a successful period in their season, losing only one of their last 11 matches in all competitions.

Athletic have won 88, drawn 42 and lost 71 of their previous 201 matches in all competitions with Espanyol, but they have actually lost the last two games between the two teams, including a 2-0 reverse in their last league fixture on May 2026.

The Lions are winless in their last three fixtures with Espanyol, but they did win three straight fixtures against the Catalan team between January 2023 and October 2024.

Espanyol entered the international break off the back of a goalless draw with Deportivo La Coruna, while their last away fixture brought a 1-0 victory over Villarreal.

The Catalan team boast a record of three wins, three draws and six defeats from their 12 matches, with 12 points leaving them in 13th spot in the division.

Eder Sarabia took charge of Espanyol at the end of October, and the immediate improvement has been obvious, claiming four points from his two league games at the helm.

Espanyol were excellent in the first half of last season and had the look of a team potentially capable of finishing in the Champions League spot, but a disappointing second half of the campaign saw them ultimately finish 11th.

The White and Blues have picked up seven points from their six away league matches this season, and they recorded a 2-1 victory over Athletic in the corresponding fixture at San Mames during the 2025-26 campaign.

Athletic Bilbao form (all competitions):.

Espanyol form (all competitions):.

Athletic will again be missing Maroan Sannadi, Gorka Guruzeta and Unai Eguiluz through injury, while Aitor Paredes and Nico Serrano are doubts at this stage of proceedings.

Unai Simon, Aymeric Laporte and Nico Williams all featured for Spain over the international break, and the trio are set to be in the starting side on Friday night.

There could also be a return to the starting side for Oihan Sancet, while Inaki Williams is likely to keep his spot through the middle for the Basque outfit.

As for Espanyol, Roger Hinojo is available again after serving a suspension against Deportivo before the international break, but Kike Garcia, Jofre Carreras and Urko Gonzalez are expected to miss out due to injury problems.

Alex Calatrava has ruptured the cruciate ligament in his left knee, meanwhile, and the attacker is facing a lengthy period out.

Roberto Fernandez has scored six times in 12 appearances for the White and Blues this season, and the 24-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There could also be a return to the side for Bryan Zaragoza, who dropped down to the bench for the clash with Deportivo.

Athletic Bilbao possible starting lineup:.

Simon; Rincon, Vivian, Laporte, Berchiche; Canales, Gerenabarrena; Berenguer, Sancet, N Williams; I Williams.

Espanyol possible starting lineup:.

Fortuno; El Hilali, Cabrera, Hartman; Dolan, Exposito, Lozano, Hinojo; Milla; Zaragoza, Fernandez.

Espanyol are capable of making this a tricky match for Athletic, but we are expecting the Basque outfit to gather a valuable three points on Friday evening.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rangers are ready to reignite their interest in former fan favourite Vaclav Cerny, with Besiktas reportedly ready to let him leave in January.

According to reports, Rangers manager Derek McInnes highlighted interest in the winger during the summer transfer window, and the Glasgow giants reportedly held discussions with his club to bring the Czech international back to Ibrox permanently.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Those talks are understood to have broken down over Besiktas’ asking price. However, Rangers are ready to return to the negotiating table when the transfer window reopens, with reports claiming the club now believes that he could be made available in January after failing to impress in Istanbul this season.

Cerny, 29, spent a successful season on loan at Rangers during the 2024/25 campaign, notching 18 goals and assisting a further nine across all competitions after being signed by Philippe Clement from Wolfsburg that summer. However, a permanent deal didn’t materialise, as the club changed ownership and named Russell Martin as the club’s new head coach.

Recent findings suggest that after leaving Rangers, he moved to the Turkish Super League instead, and performed admirably in his debut campaign at the Tupras Stadium, registering 15 goal contributions as Besiktas finished fourth. However, he hasn’t replicated that form so far this term, last scoring in a 4-1 win over Marseille in the Europa League back on September 17.

Meanwhile, on-loan Rangers winger Oscar Cortes looks set to return to the club in the fresh year, with reports claiming Huracan have turned down their option to make the deal permanent at the end of the Argentinian season, which is scheduled to end in December.

It has been revealed that cortes, 22, originally signed for Rangers on loan from Ligue 1 outfit RC Lens in February 2024, scoring once and assisting twice in his first seven appearances, before injury ended his season. After joining permanently for £4.5million at the end of the campaign, the Colombian’s injury troubles followed him into the new season, and he missed several games after developing a knee injury in the 0-0 draw with Hearts on opening day.

Industry observers note that dogged by various challenges throughout his first full season at Ibrox, he made just 10 starts and was allowed to sign on loan for Spanish second tier side Sporting Gijon. He struggled in Spain, though, failing to score in eight appearances, and had his loan cut short before moving to Huracan on a similar deal.

According to recent reports, his stint at Buenos Aires has been more successful, though. A regular in the Huracan starting XI, he has registered nine goal contributions across the season. However, despite his strong form, reports in South America say he will be allowed to return to Govan when their season ends next month, with Huracan unable to pay the Ibrox side's asking price of around £4.2million.

The fee has also scared off Atletico Nacional, who were mulling over a deal to bring him back to Colombia recently, with the club understood to have cooled their interest over Rangers’ asking price for Cortes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Saturday, Gary Mansell’s side conceded three goals in five minutes in a 3-0 defeat at Dover Athletic to exit the FA Trophy at the second-round stage.

And in midweek they slipped to another Isthmian Premier defeat, when a first-half goal by Alfie Cerulli was enough to give Brentwood a 1-0 win at Leylands Park.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The Hillians have fallen to 13th in the table and have gone seven games without a win.

They need an improvement soon and will hope to kick-start a revival when they visit Stanway Rovers for a league game on Saturday. They also visit Crowborough in the Velocity Trophy next Tuesday.

Mansell is hopeful that boosts to the squad in the form of the permanent signing of striker George Vorster and the return from injury of other key players will help breathe new life into the season.

At Dover in Saturday’s Trophy tie, three goals in a devastating five-minute spell in the first half proved decisive.

The Hillians made a positive start and Ben Pope threatened early on before a later effort came back off the post.

But Dover took the lead in the 23rd minute through Jack Bates and two minutes later Dequane Wilson-Braithwaite doubled their advantage.

When Corie Andrews added a third in the 27th minute, it felt like game over.

Hill did keep battling away and created chances to get back in it through Chris Whelpdale and Vorster – who the club are delighted to tie into a permanent contract.

Despite the disappointing result, the Hillians’ determination and effort throughout the Trophy tie could not be faulted.

Mansell said afterwards: “For 20 minutes I thought we were the better team. We had a clear game-plan that the boys executed. And we imploded for four minutes and that was game over.

It has been revealed that “We were doing well then decided to go off-script and play central passes that weren’t really on. We got beaten in transition three times and they scored three goals – they were ruthless. That cost us the game.

“In the second half we were much better and had a go.”.

Mansell said he was delighted goal ace Vorster was now a Hill player, not on loan, and thanked his previous club Slough for helping get the move sealed.

And the manager mentioned he was confident that with the way they were playing and injured personnel like Reggie Ward and Martyn Box coming back in, wins would follow.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Celtic managerial target Robbie Keane has been tipped for a surprise return to the dugout after being named a major favourite for a top EFL Championship job, with ex-Rangers and Hibs bosses also in the running.

Keane, 46, was believed to have held talks with the Celtic hierarchy over becoming the club’s new manager in the summer. However, talks broke down over fan anger at his decision to remain in charge of Israeli Premier League outfit Maccabi Tel Aviv during the outbreak of the nation’s war against Gaza, before moving to Ferencvaros in January 2025.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Out of work since quitting his role as head coach of the Hungarian side in May, the former Republic of Ireland international is now one of the leading favourites to take over at promotion-chasing side Swansea City following Vitor Matos’ decision to depart to become the new manager of Ligue 1 side Strasbourg on Tuesday.

Presently sixth in the EFL Championship table, Swansea signed former Scottish Premiership trio Stephen Welsh, Elijah Just and Ross Stewart in the summer, and had started strongly under Matos. However, despite being just three points off the automatic promotion places, the Portuguese manager opted to leave for Stade de la Meinau.

According to recent reports, while former Mainz manager Bo Henriksen is the current 5/1 favourite, Keane is joint-third on the list alongside recently sacked Manchester United boss, Michael Carrick, at 14/1. Ex-Middlesbrough and Wolverhampton Wanderers manager Rob Edwards is priced at 10/1.

Former Rangers boss Russell Martin is also among the candidates, with the current Leicester City boss having an outside chance of a sensational return to the club that he left in the summer of 2023. Appointed as head coach of Swansea in August 2021, the 40-year-old won 39 of his 99 games in charge of the club before being poached by Southampton, where he led the club to promotion via the EFL Championship playoffs.

In a recent development, even more interestingly, former Hibs head coach Paul Heckingbottom is named on the list of favourites following his sacking at Preston North End in September. The 49-year-old endured a tough eight-month spell in charge at Easter Road in 2019, but went on to achieve automatic promotion to the English Premier League in his next role with Sheffield United.

After leaving the Blades, he spent two seasons at Deepdale, but was relieved of his duties earlier this season after losing six of his first seven games. While we await the results of Mike Maignan’s tests today following his hip injury during the France-Turkey match, there’s news on the conditions of Fikayo Tomori and Ruben Loftus-Cheek, who both underwent check-ups yesterday to assess the progress of their respective muscle injuries.

Recent findings suggest that milanNews report that the defender is undoubtedly the closest to a full recovery. His recovery is progressing well, he’s already resumed individual training on the pitch, and his gradual return to the group is expected next week. That means, however, that he will miss Sunday night’s game.

It will take a while longer before we see Ruben Loftus-Cheek back on the field again, as he continues his recovery according to the originally planned schedule. Sources indicate that coral nurseries, such as this one in French Polynesia, can be used to study the resilience of the organisms in real-world settings. Credit: Alexis Rosenfeld/Getty.

With temperatures in the Pacific Ocean at record-high levels and forecasts of an extreme El Niño climate event, intense marine heatwaves are expected around the world in the coming year1,2. Scientists must prepare to study these extreme conditions now, so that managers of marine resources and decision makers can develop and implement response strategies and communities can strategy for a hotter future.

The super El Niño is cooking coral reefs — can lullabies and probiotics save them?

The super El Niño is cooking coral reefs — can lullabies and probiotics save them?

It has been revealed that el Niño is part of a recurring natural cycle in Earth’s climate in which warmer waters in the central and eastern Pacific alter ocean and atmospheric circulation, affecting weather worldwide. Marine heatwaves associated with El Niño provide opportunities to study ecosystems under real-world stress conditions and on scales that cannot be replicated in a laboratory.

Marine heatwaves can be forecast weeks or months ahead, giving researchers time to design field studies, deploy instruments and collect baseline data. Investigations can be designed to test theories and improve our understanding of ecological processes, thresholds and recovery mechanisms in a rapidly warming ocean.

It has been revealed that such knowledge can inform decisions about how to manage marine resources, such as whether to close fisheries. Much has been learnt about marine heatwaves since the last El Niño, in 2023–24 (see ‘Hot water’). But these lessons need to be consolidated and scaled up into consistent, long-term preparedness plans.

Source: Climate Reanalyzer (CC-BY-4.0); go.nature.com/4zae69a.

According to recent reports, fortunately, effective approaches established in one place can be extended to others. Australia is a leader in developing early-warning systems and response plans for adaptation to a more extreme ocean climate. Other nations (including the United Kingdom, the United States, Fresh Zealand and Peru) have improved their awareness of these events and put in place observation systems, forecasts and briefings, policy mechanisms and (in a few cases) adaptation measures.

But further action is needed, particularly in locations that have previously been unaffected by severe marine heatwaves. Here, we highlight seven priorities in increasing marine heatwave preparedness.

Seasonal forecasts with lead times of several months are now being delivered in various regions, including the United States3 and Australia4, and such systems are being developed in the United Kingdom and New Zealand5 and for the Mediterranean Sea6.

Forecasting relies on physical and statistical models to predict probable ocean temperatures7. Data from sustained surface and below-surface observations are essential for initializing models and verifying predictions, building users’ confidence in forecasts.

The super El Niño is more than a climate shock — it’s a health one, too.

The super El Niño is more than a climate shock — it’s a health one, too.

But managers want to know more precisely what the duration and intensity of a marine heatwave is expected to be. Forecasts become less accurate the further ahead they look and at fine spatial scales, such as along coasts. Improved ocean monitoring, a better understanding of the drivers of marine heatwaves and continued refinements of model physics are needed to improve forecast accuracy7.

Sources indicate that advances in machine learning are expected to be transformative. Next-generation models that incorporate ocean physics might be able to predict unprecedented marine heatwaves more accurately than current technologies can. Downscaling global climate models to inshore regions using machine-learning techniques could also increase the usefulness of forecasts in places where most marine-resource people operate.

Sources indicate that planning for and communication about impending marine heatwaves are also improving1. In 2023, engagement was piecemeal and often only in response to events that were already in progress. Activities are now more proactive and structured.

Recent findings suggest that coordinated briefings that translate forecasts into action provide ways of engaging with affected groups and planning ahead. Such communication strategies should be implemented around the world4,8. National briefings provide a broad overview of marine heatwave risks and impacts. Regional and industry specialists can provide further local advice.

Sources indicate that for example, Australia’s national marine climate briefing series4 has been running since 2023. Similar meetings (led or contributed to by some of us) have taken place for the western Pacific Ocean (G.S.) and in the United Kingdom (C.R.), Brazil (K.E.S.), Singapore (C.M.S.) and New Zealand (C.M.S.).

In a recent development, seafood-producing firms and conservation managers need a menu of actions to choose from when a marine heatwave looms. Options include adjusting collection strategies, temporarily closing fisheries and modifying aquaculture operations1.

Australia has developed regional and industry-specific response plans for marine heatwaves8. Response teams for fisheries are active during warming events and provide coordinated mechanisms for assessment, communication and management actions4,9.

Impacts of marine heatwaves are being monitored in restored giant kelp forests in Tasmania, Australia.Credit: Scott Ling/University of Tasmania.

According to recent reports, early-warning systems and interagency coordination are key components of timely responses. Industry has also adopted operating protocols to reduce the impacts of marine heatwaves on animal health and food-product quality. For example, abalone fisheries in Newly introduced South Wales have changed how sea snails (Haliotis spp.) are fished, handled and prepared for live export10. Other regions could benefit from similar plans4.

In a recent development, for example, fishing of Peruvian anchoveta (Engraulis ringens), the source of around 20% of fishmeal and fish oil globally, has already been curbed by the current El Niño. In 2023, the fishery had to be closed, resulting in an estimated loss11 of US$1.4 billion. This year, an alert in February prompted Peruvian authorities to bring the fishing season forwards by two weeks and reduce the total allowable catch of anchoveta and white anchovy (Anchoa nasus) by more than 30% to 1.9 million tonnes. This meant that fisheries could catch about 450,000 tonnes before the heatwave intensified and the season was ended in May.

According to recent reports, in 2023, marine heatwave preparedness was recognized as inadequate in most regions. The emphasis then was mainly on raising risk awareness in sectors such as fisheries and aquaculture1. However, these and other industries need to adapt to a changing ocean, too.

It has been revealed that awareness has now grown among sectors and institutions, and behaviours have begun to change. For example, Australian marine climate briefings draw engagement from aquaculture and fishery managers, marine tourism operators, policymakers, researchers and individual fishers4.

In the United States, forecasts of marine heatwaves trigger advice to fishers regarding increases in interactions with marine mammals as the overlap between animals’ hunting grounds and deployed fishing gear expands, which can result in fishery closures. Coral-reef managers involved in restoration efforts can scale back replanting efforts and start collecting genetic material.

The worst El Niño in recorded history is brewing — here’s how governments must prepare.

The worst El Niño in recorded history is brewing — here’s how governments must prepare.

In the Mediterranean Sea, limiting diving tourism at coral reefs to minimize damage during marine heatwaves has been proposed, mirroring practices that were adopted in Asia during the 2023–24 marine heatwaves11.

In the Cook Islands’ black-pearl industry, seasonal forecasts have been proposed for supporting decisions around adaptive management aimed at reducing the thermal stress of oysters. These include increased reliance on hatchery production under controlled temperature conditions and preferential harvesting of pearls during cooler periods of the year.

In the United Kingdom, a national marine heatwave network and code of best practice have been established, enabling the exchange of transdisciplinary knowledge. Similar transfers of experience, capacity and lessons learnt between jurisdictions can accelerate preparedness globally and help to embed risk management into routine decision-making processes4.

Sources indicate that the 2023 El Niño led to calls to strengthen monitoring and research capacity to improve the detection of, understanding of and response to marine heatwaves. Observation networks are now becoming a core component of preparedness and response intends, providing the information needed to support forecasting, impact assessment, management interventions and long-term adaptation strategies12.

Recent findings suggest that targeted uses of gliders and intensified monitoring strategies can bolster research, situational awareness and management decisions12. Research has expanded into understanding ecological resilience and adaptation. For example, genetic studies are identifying traits that might enhance the capacity of key fishery or habitat-forming species13 to persist under increasing thermal stress.

The Rebels looked on course for another notable away National League win when they led 1-0 at Glanford Park courtesy of Jordan Young’s fine finish in the first half.

But the Iron levelled three minutes into time added on, leaving bosses frustrated, with Adam Hinshelwood shown a red card at full-time.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Industry observers note that worthing were denied the chance of a quick return to winning form when Tuesday night’s Sussex Transport Senior Cup tie at Wick was rained off. Now the seventh-placed Reds tackle another double-game week in the league – at home to Harrogate on Saturday and away to Woking on Tuesday.

Assistant boss Jon Meeney told club media after Saturday’s draw: “It was a really good first half away from home – the lads carried out everything we desired.

"But we revealed our naivety in the second half and made it a lot harder than it needed to be, hence why we conceded a late goal.

“First half we were present in duels… dealt with their direct balls and indicated a real intensity against the ball.

"We passed the ball and got up the pitch to suffocate the opposition at times.

"But we stopped playing and stopped finding solutions in the second half. We lost a bit of bravery and went longer and the game opened up.

"We didn’t arrive on enough second balls, we were disconnected, which gave them space – and that’s the naivety of the group, and you’re going to get that with a young group.

"We’ve got to learn and we’ve got to be better at seeing out games of football in that manner.”.

Meeney praised scorer Jordan Young, saying: “We know he can be a game-changer.

"He creates but what we like about Youngy is we know he has that quality and it’s what he does off the ball.”.

In a recent development, he remarked the whole squad needed to learn the off-the-ball side of the game from the likes of Young. Meeney said there was a lot to like about the team’s overall display: “The lads have shown an honest performance, they’ve shown grit and determination, honesty to defend the box, stopping crosses, marking in the box.”.

The assistant boss described Worthing’s travelling support as ‘outstanding’ and added: “They were with the boys from minute one. It was a fantastic showing after the game applauding the boys off, and vice-versa.

"But we’re just really disappointed it was a draw – it should have been a win.".

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 10:05 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 18:02 EST, 15 November 2026.

Jarrad Branthwaite has been left out of England’s matchday squad for the Nations League decider in Spain, raising questions over his future involvement under Thomas Tuchel.

The Everton centre back’s omission means that two rivals who were not in the original squad but were added last week, Dan Burn and James Hill, are now seemingly ahead of him in the pecking order.

There was a clue as to Tuchel’s uncertainty over Branthwaite when, ahead of last Thursday's Croatia game, he revealed concerns over his suitability to England’s way of playing.

‘Jarrad Branthwaite is doing very well but it's a very different style of play for him from Everton towards us,’ mentioned the head coach.

Tuchel then selected Burn ahead of him for the 2-1 win, and mentioned: ‘You can see that Dan Burn is straight away a major voice in training and is more used to the style with Newcastle from the last two seasons with Eddie Howe, where they followed in a high press and man-to-man.’.

It had been thought that Branthwaite, 24, could emerge as a starter at left-sided centre back, given his good club form this season. That now feels unlikely, with Burn and Marc Guehi, who is right now injured, preferred by Tuchel.

Jarrad Branthwaite has been left out of the England squad for their clash against Spain.

James Hill and Dan Burn, who were both added to the England squad last week, appear to have jumped above Branthwaite in the pecking order.

Branthwaite has made two substitute appearances under the German, totalling 28 minutes. Also left out of the matchday squad for Sunday’s game in Madrid are Josh King and James Garner.

Sources indicate that everton midfielder Garner came off the bench against Croatia at Wembley and thought he had scored his first England goal, only for VAR to rule it out for offside. He now misses the chance to build on that cameo against the world champions.

It has been revealed that for King, 19, the wait for a senior debut continues after his maiden call-up, a reward for an impressive start to the season with Fulham. Tuchel was forced to trim three players from his 26-man travelling squad, with the return to fitness of defenders Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence increasing competition for places.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Rangers and Sunderland head coach Michael Beale has broken his silence on his turbulent 177-day spell in charge of Belgian Pro League side Zulte Waregem after resigning last week.

Beale, 46, brought down the curtain on his short time at the Elindus Arena following the 4-1 defeat to Sint-Truidense last week, which made it six consecutive league defeats. Their worst run of results since October 7, 2018, they are just four points above the relegation zone.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

His spell in Belgium was plagued by rumours of a breakdown in his relationship with senior figures at the club over Waregem’s direction and strategy. Beale actually started the campaign brightly, going unbeaten in their opening five games. However, their form swiftly deteriorated, and they have failed to register a victory since September 6.

His first managerial role since being sacked after just 12 games in charge at Sunderland almost three years ago, he exited Waregem with an identical record to the one he held at the Stadium of Light, with four wins, two draws, and six losses, meaning he left both sides with a 33.3% win rate after 12 games.

In a short statement confirming his departure, Waregem remarked: “After several internal discussions between the head coach and the club, both parties decided to end their collaboration by mutual agreement.” Zulte Waregem are yet to appoint Beale’s permanent successor, with interim head coach Steve Colpaert expected to take charge of their league game vs Royal Antwerp at the weekend.

Recent findings suggest that A week on from his departure, Beale penned an emotional farewell message to Waregem via his official Instagram page, writing: “Waregem, thankyou. It has been an honour and privilege to manage this club and I want to begin by thanking the fans for their incredible support. From day one, your passion and loyalty stood out and made coaching this club feel truly special. I will never forget the welcome you gave me and I have been overwhelmed by all your messages and kind words over the last few days.

“This community has become a home to me and to everyone I met in the local shops, coffee houses, parks, restaurants and bars: thank you. Many of you have become true friends and you have made me feel completely one of your own. I also want to show my gratitude to the players and staff for their hard work, dedication and the special memories we created together. You have been a pleasure to work with and I wish you every success in the future.”.

The ex-Rangers manager first joined Rangers as first-team coach during Steven Gerrard’s spell as manager at Ibrox. However, he left to join the former Liverpool icon in a similar role when he was appointed at Aston Villa in November 2021. Shortly afterwards, Beale took on his first managerial role with Queens Park Rangers.

Sources indicate that he lasted just six months at Loftus Road before being poached by Rangers as a replacement for Giovanni van Bronckhorst. He struggled in the main role at Rangers, though, and was sacked in October 2023 before joining Sunderland three months later.

Recent findings suggest that having not played at the weekend Roffey went into this game knowing a win would take them back into the play-off places. Callum Chesworth was serving a suspension, but Pat Gibbs was back in the starting line up and Dan Pearse on the bench after injury.

Roffey started well with Bailey Moyo firing over in the first minute. Two minutes later Charlie Gibson burst down the left and set up Moyo but Leather in the visitor’s goal pulled off a smart save. Roffey continued to press and after 15 minutes a well-judged pass from Pat Gibbs put Moyo in on goal, but he decided to square it and unfortunately no-one could get the final touch. Five minutes later Jordan Mase must have thought he had scored when put clear in the box, but Leather manages to tip his effort over the bar.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

After weathering the early storm Down started to grow into the game with their dangerous front two of Harley and Leslie. Leslie latched on to a long pass and poked it past Boar’s keeper Charlie Burton, but Gibbs raced back to clear the danger. In their next attack the visitors had the ball in the net, but the assistant’s flag was already up.

Recent findings suggest that down were seeing much more of the ball now and it took a great tackle from Byron Napper to stop Harley getting through on goal. Strong appeals for a penalty from the men in red were waved away by the referee. To add salt to Down’s wounds, a minute later Roffey took the lead. A fast attack resulted in a free kick that top scorer Mase curled round the wall and in for the opener. The game looked well balanced at the interval, with Roffey having seen enough of their visitor’s threat to know that one goal was probably not going to be enough.

Three minutes after the break and one became two with another cracking finish. Stan Berry got to the byline then cut back and curled the ball inside the far post to double the lead and give the Boars some breathing space. With that extra cushion Roffey began to exert more control and Down old boy Callum Kilkenny raced down the left, but his shot hit the outside of the post. The hosts continued to look for a third and Luke Harrison put in a teasing cross that managed to evade the three on rushing Boars.

Industry observers note that evan Hoarty and Luca Allen replaced Moyo and Berry with 25 minutes remaining then in the seventy second minute Kilkenny looked like he had sealed the game for Roffey. His first shot was blocked but he reacted fastest to bury the rebound. It could have been four five minutes later when a blast from Mase was brilliantly saved by Leather.

Approaching the last Ten minutes and Dan Pearse, Hayden Skerry and Teddy Wood replaced Gibson, Napper and Kilkenny. A good illustration of the quality of the Boars squad. Skerry came close as his and Mase’s efforts were cleared off the line as the Boars still looked hungry. However, it was the visitors who completed the scoring when after a foul from a cross resulted in a penalty from which Will Harley sent Burton the wrong way for a consolation goal.

So, a tricky looking fixture had been negotiated and the three goals and three points took Roffey back up into fourth place in what is becoming a rather congested pack of teams behind leaders Haywards Heath and it is the Blues from Heath that will be visiting this Saturday for what should be an exciting encounter.

Roffey: Burton, Harrison, Gibson(Pearse), Napper (Wood), Gibbs, Meeres, Caplin, Mase, Berry(Allen), Moyo(Hoarty), Kilkenny(Skerry).

Hearts’ versatile attacker Rogers Mato indicates the Tynecastle dressing room is determined to end the club’s 14-year wait for a major trophy after seeing the title slip through their fingers in the final minutes of last season.

Mato, 23, played just three league games for Hearts after arriving on an initial loan from North Macedonian outfit FK Vardar last January, but has featured regularly for the Gorgie side this season after making his move permanent in the summer by penning a three-year contract in July.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sources indicate that originally signed as a wide forward, the Ugandan international was deployed as a left-back against Turkish outfit Trabzonspor in the Europa League earlier this month, with Hearts’ injury crisis seeing Mato pitted against former Liverpool icon, Mo Salah. However, he admits it’s another ex-Anfield hero, Senegal international Sadio Mane, that he takes inspiration from as he looks ahead to the African Cup of Nations in his homeland next summer.

“I grew up just watching the other players on TV and sneaking in the stadiums,” Mato told RG. “I didn't even have a chance to be like a ball boy to give them the balls in the national team. I only did that on the club level. But wearing the national team jersey is a significant responsibility, we're representing our families, our dream, and millions of Ugandans.

Recent findings suggest that “Mane is my all-time favourite African player. I would love to wear the captain's armband. I would love to lead my country. We grow by responsibilities, not by age. So, that would have a massive impact and would be a massive confidence booster for me to be leading the nation to glory.”.

The 23-year-old indicates he is using the pain of defeat to fuel another of his major dreams - bringing silverware at Tynecastle. Refusing to concede his side are out of the title race this season despite being 11 points behind league leaders Celtic, he admits the crushing way that a first top flight title win since 1960 trophy was ripped from their grasp by two late Hoops goal on the final day last season still stings.

“It's been ups and downs [since joining Hearts],” he admits. “Coming from Macedonia, playing 90-plus minutes and then coming on for Hearts and playing for 13 minutes in three games and 13 minutes in the second half of the season. It's been ups and downs, but with patience, everything will come to an end.

“I just had to come here and wait for my time, but every time we just have to be patient. I needed to work hard on myself, work hard for the team, so I can get more game time. It's all about mentality. You have to adapt to any coach that comes your way. If you don't adapt, you're dead as a footballer. Last season was hectic and brutal for the team, for the fans. Those last minutes [vs Celtic], it was a heartbreak for everyone, for every Hearts fan. It was a total disaster.

Industry observers note that “But we're looking forward to give it all this season. But suddenly we got a lot of injuries here and there, but those who are still fit, we're trying our best to still keep [the title race] alive for our friends, our brothers who are injured, so they can come and join us [when they're back]. Because we can't let it down, we still have to keep the hopes for the first place.".

Breaking: Man Utd transfer news: Red Devils to consider legal action over JJ Gabriel's Real Madrid move?

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (372 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Saikat Mandal | 18 Nov 2026 12:44.
  • Manchester United are reportedly prepared to take legal action over JJ Gabriel's proposed move to Real Madrid if they uncover any evidence of inducement.
  • Gabriel revealed back in September that he wanted to leave Old Trafford after failing to break into the senior team.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 18 Nov 2026 12:44.

Manchester United are reportedly prepared to take legal action over JJ Gabriel's proposed move to Real Madrid if they uncover any evidence of inducement.

Gabriel revealed back in September that he wanted to leave Old Trafford after failing to break into the senior team.

Although he remains registered with the club until the end of the season, that would not prevent him from moving elsewhere in the European Union once he turns 16.

A host of clubs were interested in signing the youngster, but it now appears that he is set to join Real Madrid.

Gabriel posted a farewell message to Man Utd supporters, thanking the club for their role in his development, but the Red Devils are understood to be angered by his decision.

According to the Manchester Evening News, the Red Devils were disappointed that the video was posted without any prior contact from Gabriel's representatives.

Man Utd have reportedly made several attempts to check on the teenager's welfare since he requested to leave, but have been unable to establish contact with his family.

Meanwhile, agency Epic Sports has become Gabriel's new representative, with the club believing that the youngster has been poorly advised by his father throughout the process.

The Red Devils are prepared to explore every available legal avenue should evidence of inducement from Madrid emerge, given the strict regulations surrounding the recruitment of players under the age of 18.

The youngster only turned 16 on October 6, and there was little reason to believe that his pathway to the first team would have been blocked at Old Trafford.

Critics may argue that Man Utd could have handled his development better, perhaps following Barcelona's approach with Lamine Yamal, although such success stories are relatively rare.

What appears particularly surprising is Gabriel's decision to join Real Madrid, where he would face competition from the likes of Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior, Arda Guler, Endrick and Yan Diomande for a place in the senior side.

Man Utd can hardly be held solely responsible for his decision, but the way this saga has unfolded could raise questions about the club's ability to retain and nurture its most promising young talents.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The chairman and co-owner of the club has remained silent during this rough period for the club which has seen the sacking of Colin Kazim-Richards, an embarrassing FA Cup exit to seventh tier Wimborne Town, the club rooted to bottom of League Two and interim boss Kevin Blackwell give a damning verdict on the club’s recruitment.

It’s now been a month since Kazim-Richards went and fans are unclear where the club is with the appointment.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Khalili held a fans forum in February and gave an interview to the Crawley Observer/SussexWorld in January, but noone has heard from him since – in a period that has seen Scott Lindsey sacked and another squad overhaul.

This publication has requested interviews and so has the BBC’s Robin Grey – but nothing has transpired yet.

Fans have been calling for him to say something and now former Reds Scott Malone and Tony Vessey have both noted he should say something.

Speaking on the Crawley Town podcast on the BBC with Robin, the pair spoke about about the current situation what Khalili should be doing.

Former defender Malone, who is at the moment playing for Three Bridges in the Isthmian Premier, mentioned: “There's no one else attached to the club permanently to say anything apart from Raph.

“And he's not doing it. In my opinion, he should front up because at the end of the day, he's the substantial boss. He's the owner.

“If there's no one else to do it, he should come out and do it himself. Or is there nothing to say? I'd suggest that there isn't anything to say, otherwise he'd have come out and said it. But come out and say it if there's nothing to say. At least do that.”.

And Vessey, who has been captain and manager at Crawley, agreed. “It’s been four weeks of silence, pretty much. Just be honest. People just want you to be honest with them.

Say something like ‘we're trying to recruit because of the position we're in, we're finding it a bit difficult’. ‘We're relying on Kevin Blackwell to hopefully improve that position so that we can get a permanent appointment’. I think most people would accept that. You own the club.

“You've taken on that responsibility of guiding it. So guide it. And in any business, communication is key. So football's a business. You want your supporters to turn up week in, week out, then communicate with them. And I think that's an imperative for anybody.”.

Vessey added: “If he's a businessman,then communication is key in most businesses. So he should understand that keeping everybody on side is the way forward, not to be completely silent.”.

Khalili took over leadership of the club in August 2025 as KB Sports and Leisure but was previously a minority shareholder when WAGMI were in charge.

You can listen to the full podcast on BBC Sounds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

According to recent reports, it was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”.

Matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8.

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

“It was an outstanding performance,” the manager said. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”.

The win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

As for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the new arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

It has been revealed that even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

It has been revealed that ellis Simms off the bench with a big impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV.

You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

Industry observers note that it was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

A win for Newcastle United this evening will take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to fourth in the Premier League and vindicate the members of the club’s hierarchy who insisted they had appointed an elite manager to replace Eddie Howe.

It will also suggest they got their summer rebuild right and everything will point to an exciting future for a newly introduced look team.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

That may seem like an odd thing to write given how wildly different those reactions are but that is where Newcastle find themselves at the moment. We do not actually know if they are any good or what the expectations should be for a young team with a rookie Premier League head coach.

There remains an undercurrent of anxiety among supporters who have seen so many of their best players leave over the last 12 months and be replaced by young, emerging talent from across Europe.

Recent findings suggest that the 4-1 thrashing at Leeds in their last away game was a painful reminder of the team’s vulnerability. They were bullied and outclassed.

Newcastle have not put together an impressive 90-minute performance since the opening day draw with Liverpool, yet that defeat to Leeds was also the only game they have lost. in all competitions. We will know a lot more about them after this. This is a game they are expected to win, so the ramifications of a defeat will be more severe.

When Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

In a recent development, so Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

Industry observers note that “You know what they came up with?” Kilcline notes. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

It has been revealed that today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

Frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. Tino Livramento pulled out of the England camp with injury and is likely to be sidelined for a while longer but Matthias Jaissle was more optimistic about his raft of other doubts: William Osula, Lewis Miley, Amar Dedic, club captain Dan Burn, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey.

Latest Update: Chelsea news: Manager merry-go-round exposes flaws of BlueCo model at Strasbourg

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (531 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 12:46.
  • Has Strasbourg become a prisoner of BlueCo’s strategy?
  • It has been revealed that only 13th in Ligue 1 with 10 points after 10 games, Strasbourg are going through a very difficult start to the season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 12:46.

Has Strasbourg become a prisoner of BlueCo’s strategy? The departure of Hugo Oliveira, replaced by Vitor Matos after only a few months in the dugout, has reignited questions over the management of the Alsatian club.

It has been revealed that only 13th in Ligue 1 with 10 points after 10 games, Strasbourg are going through a very difficult start to the season. But beyond the results, it is above all the absence of continuity that stands out. Since January, four managers have followed one another in the Strasbourg dugout. Such instability is hard to reconcile with building a genuine sporting project.

Recent findings suggest that liam Rosenior’s departure for Chelsea last January had already given a glimpse of the limits of the model. The Englishman, now at Paris FC, had established a playing identity and allowed Strasbourg to rediscover a certain ambition, before being called up to the flagship club of the BlueCo galaxy.

Gary O’Neil succeeded him, before joining Ipswich Town a few months later. Hugo Oliveira, who arrived this summer, ultimately lasted only four months. Vitor Matos is now expected to succeed him.

This succession of changes raises an obvious question: how do you build a team when its manager changes so regularly?

Recent findings suggest that each coach arrives with his own principles, tactical preferences and recruitment needs. Rosenior’s high press, O’Neil’s orientations and Oliveira’s intentions have not allowed lasting continuity to be established. Strasbourg’s players constantly have to adapt, while collective automatisms are called into question.

The transfer window does not help matters. Strasbourg had a particularly busy summer, with a multitude of movements, including several players from the Chelsea ecosystem.

According to recent reports, the club sometimes looks more like a piece in a vast player circulation system than one building its squad around clearly identified needs. Strasbourg’s sporting logic therefore seems regularly to come second to that of BlueCo.

Sources indicate that it would be unfair, though, to deny the benefits of this policy: Strasbourg have rediscovered a European dimension and reached the semi-finals of the Conference League in spring 2026. The club also has a young squad with resale value, and has the resources to attract promising talent.

Recent findings suggest that but what is the point of developing players if the best of them are liable to leave as soon as an opportunity arises within the group? What is the point of investing in a manager if he can be replaced so promptly?

Rosenior’s departures and the player movements between Strasbourg and Chelsea illustrate this difficulty in preserving a trajectory of the club’s own.

BlueCo has found in Alsace a tremendous breeding ground for its young talents. But Strasbourg cannot be reduced to a development centre at the service of Chelsea.

The French club’s supporters expect a team to identify with, a readable project and ambitions that do not change with the owner’s needs. By treating Strasbourg as an interchangeable element of its organisation, BlueCo risks weakening exactly what gives the club its value: its identity. Unless it is already too late? Strasbourg would benefit from disengaging from this stifling structure.

Tech Report: Senior Cup exit is a setback for Bognor Regis Town – but bigger picture looks rosy

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1212 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co
