📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Danny Hollands’ side went out after a 3-2 reverse to the SCFL outfit, meaning the Rocks are now out of all the cup competitions.
  • The loss came on the back of a 2-1 derby day victory over Littlehampton Town in the Isthmian South Central division on Saturday.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Danny Hollands’ side went out after a 3-2 reverse to the SCFL outfit, meaning the Rocks are now out of all the cup competitions.

The loss came on the back of a 2-1 derby day victory over Littlehampton Town in the Isthmian South Central division on Saturday. And the Nye Camp aces get the chance to improve their points tally on Saturday when they host Hayes & Yeading.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The victory – after two reverses on the spin -- against the lowly Sportsfield outfit maintained the club’s spot in third in the league standings, with Egham Town top and Jersey Bulls, who the Rocks visit next week, second.

Another positive to come out of that game was the full return of striker Cal Laycock after a long lay-off -- and similarly against United a bonus was the goal-scoring return of long-term absentee Billy Allcock.

It was assistant manager Ben Kneller who spoke to the club’s YouTube channel about the cup exit to Eastbourne, against whom youngsters such as Dennis Wooldridge, Noah Light, Toby Kingswell, Archie Bennett and Louie Williams all featured -- and some of those had actually played the night before in an U18s game, too.

Kneller remarked: “We need to keep moving forward but all in all, if we were stood here having the conversation last year when we first game (to manage) and we said, 'listen, we are going to be third or fourth in the league come mid-November, we have lost two games in 26, but you're out of the cups, would you have taken it? You probably would have done. We need to step back to see where we are, (compared) to where we were.

In a recent development, "It was a little bit of real reality check after Saturday when we had 1,300 in (and beat our local rivals). We are not happy to be out and not happy with a few in the dressing room – but there are positives within the negatives.

Recent findings suggest that "Noah is a very intelligent footballer (for instance). They (some u18s) train with us on a Thursday and they are around the environment all the time and just because they don't feature in games they are still in around along with others.

“We want to progress young players in the area and that is what Bognor is all about. It's not all about winning this and winning that, it is very much about building from the base and we believe in that. From our side of things there is a pathway for the 18s and we have shown it.".

On being out of all the cups, he added: "We would like to have a cup run but you can never guarantee it but we would have liked to deliver it Maybe we strip the squad back a little more now we are out of the cups and we realign.".

Here’s Liam Goodley’s full report from the Senior Cup defeat.

Bognor were knocked out of the Sussex Senior Cup under the lights at Nyewood Lane as their makeshift side were put to the test by well organised, Eastbourne United.

According to recent reports, tommy Block went into the book early on for his challenge after a back pass. Rhyle Overden crossed it in from the free-kick but straight into the arms of Archie Bennett in the Bognor goal.

Charlie Gunson latched on to a loose ball after a long ball into the area and his strike was deflected away from the back legs of a defender on 11 minutes. Archie Bennett did well to stop two players twice after James Hull's cross that was hit low into the box on 15 minutes, keeping the scoreline goalless.

Sources indicate that gunson did well to wind into the box but his shot was deflected into the path of Ollie Lovell who was also denied by an Eastbourne body. Joe Overy did well on the attack for the visitors. He cut inside after some swift passing play but fired it over the crossbar from outside the area.

Anderson hooked the ball high into the area from the freekick. Block was unmarked as he leapt up to head that towards goal. The ball looped up kindly for the goalkeeper though.

In a recent development, sorge Nones did all the hard work winding his way through the area but blasted over the bar with his left foot on 37 minutes. Secka had to punch away a dipping direct freekick frm Gunson off the left side on 41 minutes. HT 0-0.

Changes at half-time saw Block, Benny Read and Gunson come off for Josh Batt, Toby Kingswell and Ethan Robb. Batt got the ball forward to Louie Williams, but after rounding his marker he fired it low and into the grateful arms of Secka from a tight angle on 54 minutes.

Bognor made another change on 60 minutes that saw Maadhav Jagota replaced by Callum Laycock and Lovell came off for Billy Allcock.

Industry observers note that A swift move down the left saw Eastbourne United take the lead on 67 minutes. Overy used his pace to run down the left before diverting a low ball into the area and ex-Rock Callum Barlow knocked it in from close range.

Williams set Kingswell on his way down the right wing but Kingswell smacked his cross out of play for a goal kick in a poor half for Bognor.

Robb's free-kick curled dangerously into the area on 78 minutes. The ball was knocked down wide of the right post as the goalkeeper watched it roll past the right post.

James Stone, off the bench, did really well to compose himself running in front of defence before powerfully driving the ball into the net beyond a diving Bennett on 79 minutes, extending United's lead.

Harvey Whyte put in a great delivery from the right and Laycock got their ahead of his marker to get something onto it, and managed to divert the ball low, of which Secka managed to save low to his right.

Another forward ball saw Billy Allcock run through and his first strike was blocked before he followed up to net it on the rebound on 84 minutes for 2-1.

However, that reduced lead didn't last long as Stone worked hard on the right before putting it on a plate for Overy to knock into the net on 85 minutes.

According to recent reports, bognor got another goal back direct from Robb's corner as Laycock netted it with his head on 91 minutes. Bognor were attacking towards the end for a last gasp equaliser but Eastbourne United were good defensively to stave off the danger late on.

So the Rocks were knocked out of the Sussex Senior Cup at the third round stage and are now able to fully focus on their league campaign with some massive games coming up, including next up, a home tie against Hayes & Yeading United this Saturday (21st November, 3pm).

Recent findings suggest that rocks: Bennett, Read, Wooldridge, Anderson, Whyte, Block, Jagota, Lovell, Williams, Gunson, Light. Subs (all used): Batt, Laycock, Allcock, Robb, Kingswell.

Ben Royall (2), Ollie Rawlins (2), Zac Young and Charlie Connell scored to put Chris Simmons’ side into the quarter-finals.

Simmons said: “It was a great result for us in what could have been a really tricky game. They are a very good side and ready to push on to step four but they didn’t take the early chances they had and we were really clinical.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

“They should have been a goal in front from a mistake by us, then within 30 seconds we were 1-0 up.

“The wet/sticky surface made it difficult for both sides who looked to play but overall I think the neutrals got their money’s worth.

“It was nice to make five changes from Saturday, get minutes into lads returning from injury and reach the quarter-finals.

“The league is our priority but everyone loves a cup run.”.

It has been revealed that it completed a perfect week for the Bears after Saturday’s 2-0 Isthmian South East win at Margate, in which Luke Bejashvili scored both. Heath host Hastings on Saturday.

Here is Andrew Crisp’s Heath v Heath match report….

On paper this midweek trip to Southern Combination League leaders Haywards Heath Town looked a potential banana skin for Chris Simmons’ Broadbridge Heath.

The hosts may be a division below the Bears but they have made a great start to the season, five points clear at the top of the Premier Division, unbeaten at home after ten matches and having knocked cup favourites Brighton & Hove Albion out by 2-0 in an earlier round, but things don’t always work out as some may predict.

Simmons made five changes to the starting line-up that won 2-0 at Margate three days earlier, four at the back including Bailey Cotton on his way back from injury and making his first start since September and Ollie Rawlins making just his second start of the season after injury.

Broadbridge Heath got off to a great start on 3 minutes when Ben Holden received the ball on the halfway line and drove forward into the Haywards Heath half before playing the ball out wide to Ben Royall advancing down the left, and the Bears full-back cut inside and struck a low right foot shot from distance into the bottom right corner of the net.

The Bears doubled their lead on 24 minutes with Holden and Royal involved again: this time Holden, in the centre of the park, played the ball into the feet of Royall with his back to goal and closely marked, the Bears defender turned his marker and ran towards the Haywards Heath penalty area before striking a low left foot shot across the goal into the far corner.

At the other end Jack Barnes powered a header from a corner onto the top of the crossbar and Bears skipper Brad Peters reacted quickly to clear the ball off the goal-line but it was Broadbridge Heath who increased their lead on 32 minutes.

An interchange of passes ended with Luke Bejashvili playing the ball into the feet of Holden who played a first time pass to Ollie Rawlins some 25 yards out and with his back to goal and the Heath striker turned sharply to power a right foot shot into the bottom right corner giving the hosts’ keeper Charlie Roberts no chance of stopping.

Minutes later Broadbridge Heath’s Sal Marino played a defence-splitting ball to send Charlie Connell through on goal but Roberts was off his line promptly to force the player wide of goal and instead Connell played the ball back into the path of Rawlins on the edge of the “D” who blasted his shot high and wide.

A minute before the break the hosts pulled a goal back when Josh Wright crossed the ball from the right flank into the Broadbridge Heath penalty area where the ball bobbled around the six yard box before falling kindly to Charlie Meehan to tap in from close range.

Broadbridge Heath restored their three goal advantage almost immediately when a long ball was played down the left channel and chased down by Rawlins who delivered a left foot cross into the path of Zac Young, who hit a sweet left foot shot from 12 yards which was saved brilliantly by Roberts. Young pounced on the loose ball and was brought down by a clumsy challenge, and the match referee immediately pointed to the penalty spot with nobody from Haywards Heath questioning the decision and Young got up to convert the spot kick for his sixth goal of the season to make it 1-4 at the break.

Industry observers note that haywards Heath needed an early second half goal to get back into the game but the reverse happened 2 minutes into the restart when Broadbridge Heath goalkeeper Stan Williamson intercepted a right wing cross and threw the ball out swiftly to Young in the centre of the park. He drove forward to the halfway line before playing the ball wide right to Charlie Connell, who took the ball towards the goal-line and then delivered a right wing pass across the goal to Rawlins to score from six yards.

Heath added a sixth goal on the hour mark when Rawlins received the ball wide on the right and played a long ball towards the far post where it was headed in by Connell from 8 yards to near enough secure the win for the Bears.

Simmons was able to swap his players around which included the welcome return to the side for Mason Doughty, the Heath striker with eight goals from 13 games this season has missed the last eight games through injury.

Haywards Heath added a second in time added-on when a combination of Wright and Barnes won the ball off a Bears defender and linked up well down the right channel before the ball was played inside to Barnes who finished with aplomb.

BBH: Williamson, Cotton (Thiselton 60), Royall, Marino, Peters, Salaam (Richardson 65), Bejashvili, Holden, Rawlins (Doughty 70), Connell (Hards 61), Young.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 12:53.
  • Aston Villa have reportedly identified AC Milan midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek as a potential winter transfer target.
  • Earlier on Wednesday, Villa declared that one of their current engine-room options had penned a latest long-term contract.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 12:53.

Aston Villa have reportedly identified AC Milan midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek as a potential winter transfer target.

Earlier on Wednesday, Villa declared that one of their current engine-room options had penned a latest long-term contract.

Unai Emery is also not short of players for that position, with Boubacar Kamara, Joao Gomes, Leon Goretzka and Ross Barkley earning regular minutes.

Nevertheless, not helped by the inconsistent performances and individual mistakes of some of those aforementioned players, Villa remain off the pace in the Premier League.

According to Calciomercato, Loftus-Cheek has emerged as a possible option for the turn of the year.

The report alleges that Villa Park is viewed as a 'potential destination' for the former Chelsea midfielder.

Loftus-Cheek contributed 13 goals and 18 assists from his 155 appearances in a Blues shirt, but he has been at San Siro since the summer of 2023.

His stint at AC Milan can be viewed as a relative success, with 13 goals and four assists coming from 109 outings for the Italian giants.

However, the 11-cap England international's contract is due to expire at the end of the season, putting him in a position where he could leave on a free transfer in the summer.

Milan are open to cashing in on the 30-year-old in order to free up transfer funds and space on their wage bill.

Ruben Amorim's side have also won their last two matches against Inter Milan and Genoa, games which Loftus-Cheek missed through injury.

Despite Loftus-Cheek possessing qualities that Emery arguably lacks within his squad, a move to Villa makes little sense for the player.

Villa already have too many options in the number six, eight and 10 positions in Emery's familiar 4-2-3-1 or 4-4-1-1 formations.

Although Tammy Abraham has been linked with an exit from Villa, it seems unlikely that Loftus-Cheek would transition into a backup number nine behind Nicolas Jackson and Brian Madjo at this point of his career.

And there was no ‘cup-set’ on the day with Salisbury running out 4-0 winners.

On Tuesday nighr the boot was on the other foot as City were the team looking to avoid a shock when they went to SCFL Premier side Hassocks in round three of the Sussex Transport Senior Cup.

A professional and clinical display at the Beacon ended with Chi winning 6-0 to reach the last eight of a competition that ends with an Amex Stadium final.

Two goals apiece by Emmett Dunn, Isaac Bello and top scorer Harry Bridle secured the quarter-final spot.

It was the last of a relentless run of midweek matches that have stretched City’s small squad – and the coaching staff are looking forward to a couple of game-free Tuesdays when they can work on rest, recovery and other challenges.

Killpartrick noted: “We have no complaints about the outcome at Salisbury. They’re an extremely good side, very fit and played the conditions better than us.

"We kept battling and highlighted fighting spirit, which is all you can ask sometimes.

According to recent reports, "You have to take into account the difference between the two clubs. They’ve been training in Kuwait, we’ve been training at Oaklands Park – and I’m not knocking Oaklands Park, by the way!

Sources indicate that "At Hassocks we were very, very professional. We had to be and we were because that could have been a tricky tie.

"We brought in three from our B team and another youngster and were pleased with the performance and professionalism of the whole squad.".

Meanwhile after a run of seven away games in ten matches, seventh-placed City are back at Oaklands Park this Saturday to take on 14th-placed Basingstoke in a Southern League Premier South game.

After their last home match, versus Bath City, drew more than 600, they would love another major crowd in – on the day when the city centre stages its lights switch-on just after the end of the match.

Killpartrick said: “We’ve had some really entertaining home games and will aim for another.”.

Industry News: Architecture of a portal complex embedded in the poxvirus core

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (478 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, gene transcription within the viral core is a distinctive feature of poxvirus replication.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, gene transcription within the viral core is a distinctive feature of poxvirus replication. Following entry into the cytoplasm, the poxvirus core dissociates from the lateral bodies and undergoes expansion, functioning as a compartment for early transcription1. However, how molecules are exchanged between the viral core and the host cytoplasm remains poorly understood. Here, using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging, we determine the structures of the portal complex and its central pore on the vaccinia virus core at 6.7 Å and 4.4 Å resolution, respectively. Guided by structural predictions and experimental density, we identify three viral proteins, E8, E6 and L3, as the principal components of the pore and construct a structural model of their organization. The pore contains a narrow, positively charged constriction formed by conserved lysine residues in L3, substitutions of which impair viral gene expression and propagation. The dimensions and electrostatic properties of the channel are consistent with a potential role in molecular exchange across the core wall. Together, our findings establish a structural framework for understanding the organization and potential function of the poxvirus portal complex.

Tickets will be honoured for the rearranged fixture – which has now been set for Tuesday, December 1 (7.30pm) – and Dragons boss Baldwin stated: ‘We worked so hard to get the game on and were happy to go ahead.

Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it

📅 13 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3710 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.
  • In a recent development, this two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic.
  • In a recent development, the goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

In a recent development, this two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

In a recent development, the goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

Industry observers note that “I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman mentioned. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

Recent findings suggest that “We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”.

Industry observers note that avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

Industry observers note that it had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an concern for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

In a recent development, it did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Sources indicate that greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

England thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

Recent findings suggest that ioanna Papatheodorou nearly gave Greece the lead when she dribbled past Esme Morgan and Leah Williamson with ease but her powerful strike hit the crossbar. It was a let-off for England, but they made it count by taking the lead just before half-time.

Recent findings suggest that A fine team move ended with an excellent Stanway finish. It was her fifth goal in this qualifying campaign and she is England’s top scorer for 2025-26.

It has been revealed that le Tissier scored England’s second just past the hour mark before Alessia Russo made it 3-0 four minutes later. It appeared the floodgates may have opened but that proved to be a false dawn, with Greece scoring a deserved goal through Kallisti Brouksair after some poor England defending.

According to recent reports, while this game will go down as largely forgettable, it will be remembered by 18-year-old Erica Meg Parkinson and Grace Fisk, 28, who came on for their senior debuts in the closing stages. It also means Parkinson, who could have played for Japan, Portugal or Singapore, is now tied to England.

She is an exciting player for the future but will feel she has a chance of making a World Cup squad, should England get there. For now, they are taking the slow route.

That’s it for tonight. Let’s hope England can repeat the feat next week.

Stanway is looking to make life difficult for Greece next week, explaining: “We will reflect on that, see where we can minimise them as much as possible, see where we can stop the transition and stop it a little bit earlier and not give them a little bit of a lifeline.”.

According to recent reports, maya le Tissier tells ITV: “I didn’t really know it went in to be honest because I thought the keeper saved it. I just smacked it so I’m very glad. It’s always good to get your first goal, so very happy.

Sources indicate that “Not really [a moment she had dreamt about] to be honest because I’m a defender and I thought I’d just be stopping it but it’s always good to get up there. When I play that position, I find myself a little bit higher up, definitely something to work on but very happy to score my first goal.

“I do [like playing that position], I love defending as well. It’s obviously a bit different for me up there but I always try and give my best whatever position I play so I did enjoy it.”.

Georgia Stanway was left enthused by a performance which saw players fit in where they were asked, rather than where they are accustomed to playing.

Erica Meg Parkinson, one of England’s newly introduced midfielders, was apparently named after Eric Cantona.

While Cantona still famously is proud of his kung fu kick, when he attacked an obnoxious Crystal Palace fan, Parkison is less enthused by football’s most famous case of breaking the fourth wall.

Recent findings suggest that “My dad is a huge Man United fan so I was named after Eric Cantona,” Parkinson notes. “It’s a pretty good player to be named after except for, you know, the karate kicks.

“My brother was named after Denis Law. I don’t think my mum had much of a say in the name so she was dragged into it, but it kind of worked out because we both play football now.”.

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

It has been revealed that “Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”.

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

According to recent reports, “When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman mentioned. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

“That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

The Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

Sources indicate that all eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”.

Recent findings suggest that toone promptly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”.

Recent findings suggest that that opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven big-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

AFCON 2027: The nine countries already qualified for the tournament

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that the first qualified teams for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are already known.
  • It has been revealed that with four of the six qualifying matchdays played, nine of the 24 qualified nations for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are already known.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 12:59.

Sources indicate that the first qualified teams for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are already known. The tournament is scheduled for 19 June to 17 July 2027 in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

It has been revealed that with four of the six qualifying matchdays played, nine of the 24 qualified nations for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are already known. Here are all the countries that have qualified.

After the three host nations, who qualify automatically although they are taking part in the qualifiers, the fourth matchday of the 2027 qualifying campaign revealed six new qualified teams on 17 November 2026.

The co-host of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations is having a very mixed qualifying campaign. Benni McCarthy’s side did snatch a good point in South Africa (2-2), but they have only two points after four matchdays and had a scare at home against modest Eritrea (1-1).

Of the three host nations, Uganda are undoubtedly the ones having the best qualifying campaign, and the only ones to have won a match, a 1-0 victory over Libya. They are unbeaten after four matchdays and top their group ahead of Libya, Botswana and Tunisia.

Recent findings suggest that the last of these automatically qualified nations, Tanzania have not necessarily made a strong impression. They have only two points after four matchdays, but they have just held Nigeria to a 0-0 draw, their best performance of the campaign so far.

According to recent reports, one by one, the spots are being claimed! Here's who's qualified for #TotalEnergiesAFCON2027 after Matchday 4. ? https://t.co/uUJmkEBOVX.

Recent findings suggest that while waiting for the Court of Arbitration for Sport to rule on their status as 2025 champions or finalists, Senegal became the first team to secure their place at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations on the pitch. After a laboured start in Mozambique (1-1), Patrick Vieira’s side strung together three wins, over Ethiopia and then Sudan twice, to confirm their ticket 24 hours after their matchday four game, thanks to a favourable result for Mozambique.

Held by Benin (1-1) in their opening game, Burkina Faso, round of 16 finalists in the last two editions, then dropped no more points, beating Central African Republic and then Mauritania twice. Amir Abdou’s side needed only four matchdays to qualify.

Industry observers note that round of 16 finalists in 2025, Benin will be present again for the Pamoja edition. After taking a good point from their trip to Burkina Faso (1-1), Gernot Rohr’s side dictated terms to Mauritania and then Central African Republic twice to secure qualification in November 2026, following Burkina Faso’s win over Mauritania.

After reaching the quarter-finals of the previous edition, Cameroon are taking these qualifiers very seriously. Held only in Congo, David Pagou’s side beat Comoros and Namibia twice to qualify after four matchdays, following Congo’s 1-0 defeat to Comoros.

Keen to go further than the quarter-finals, the ceiling reached in the last two editions, Mali confirmed their ambitions by being the only team along with Morocco to maintain a perfect record after four matchdays. World Cup-bound Cape Verde, Liberia and Rwanda twice all fell to Anthony Da Silva’s side, who qualified thanks to these wins.

As formidable as ever in these qualifiers, Morocco have a perfect 4/4 record, having beaten Gabon, Lesotho and then Niger twice. It was the second win over Niger, 1-0, thanks to a record-breaking goal from Abdellah Ouazane, that allowed Mohamed Ouahbi’s side to qualify.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Premier League and EFL are set to hold serious conversations about the blackout’s future next year with pretty much every TV slot now exhausted.

Removing the blackout – which is a rule that prevents live football matches from being broadcast on television or streaming services between 2.45pm and 5.15pm on Saturdays – could have a detrimental effect on attendances and finances, especially clubs in the lower tiers like Crawley Town.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The blackout is under threat and television rights deals for the Premier League, EFL and Scottish Premiership are all up for renewal in 2029-30 and last year, Premier League chief executive Richard Masters stated there were no intends to remove the blackout – introduced in 2003 by UEFA as Article 48.

But this summer there appeared to be a shift in emphasis, with Masters saying there would be talks with the EFL ahead of the renewal of TV rights. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has urged caution and suggested the health of the football pyramid should come first.

The only leagues that apply Article 48 are England, Scotland and Northern Ireland. No other major country qualifies for the blackout - it is a tradition that is unique to football in the United Kingdom.

But how would it affect Crawley Town?

CEO Allman gave his personal opinion – and not necessarily that of the club – about the situation and what it would mean if it ended.

Sources indicate that he stated: “My personal opinion is that the 3pm blackout currently works well in protecting the current football pyramid. I hear the arguments about it not being in place in other countries, but there is no pyramid like the UK pyramid so am not sure it is a fair comparison.

"We see notable increases in attendances during international breaks as well as drop offs for Tuesday night games for example where they are available on SkySports+ so in general, whilst removing the blackout, would arguably increase the exposure of clubs like Crawley, would levy that with actual attendances dropping off, which whilst having the obvious financial implication, will also have impacts on atmospheres and the general match-day feel.”.

So it’s clear whether he would oppose the ending of the blackout? “I wouldn’t be in favour - as I say, I think the pyramid is what stands us apart from other countries and sports, and with that, would encourage fans to go out and experience the full pyramid, rather than looking for more Premier League games on TV.”.

He added: “Whilst I understand the argument of increased coverage, I wouldn’t levy that against supporters being in the stadium, buying a pint, eating a burger, cheering their team on and in turn, financially supporting the club to allow us to kick on across the board.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Bayern Munich can take a lead in the race for the Bundesliga title on Friday, when they welcome FC Koln to Allianz Arena.
  • The hosts are level on 21 points with second-placed Borussia Dortmund, who play on Saturday, whereas Koln are 15th with nine points after nine matchweeks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 18 Nov 2026 13:05.

Bayern Munich can take a lead in the race for the Bundesliga title on Friday, when they welcome FC Koln to Allianz Arena.

The hosts are level on 21 points with second-placed Borussia Dortmund, who play on Saturday, whereas Koln are 15th with nine points after nine matchweeks.

Prior to the start of the November international break, Bayern emerged as 2-1 victors against Mainz 05, though they were wasteful in the final third, missing three of their four major chances while scoring just two of their 26 shots.

That win was their fourth in five games in all competitions, but it will be a concern that the team have only kept one clean sheet in their last eight matches.

The Bavarians have conceded 17 goals in their 16 fixtures this season, whereas they only conceded 13 times in the corresponding period in 2025-26.

Fans will hope the expected return of Vincent Kompany, who has not been in the dugout for his side's last five fixtures since collapsing on October 23, will help boost the team's performances at the back.

Bayern have drawn two of their three most recent contests at Allianz Arena, though they are yet to experience defeat at home, winning five of their seven clashes when playing as hosts.

Kompany's side have averaged five goals per game at home in the Bundesliga, while they only conceded four goals in their four league outings at Allianz Arena.

Koln were beaten 2-1 by Bayer Leverkusen on November 8 before the start of the international break, and it will concern supporters that the club have now won just one of their past eight top-flight games (W1, D4, L3).

Manager Rene Wagner will want his team to improve considerably in the final third given they have netted just twice in their last four league fixtures, blanking on two occasions.

A defeat on Friday would leave the visitors as low as 17th should Union Berlin and Schalke 04 claim three points in matchday 10, though it should be noted that only three points separate them from eighth-placed Stuttgart.

The Billy Goats' record against Bayern is predictably poor, with Wagner's side last beating their hosts in February 2011, and another loss would be their 22nd defeat in 24 meetings.

Koln's solitary victory in their five away matches this campaign came in the DFB-Pokal against Wurzburger Kickers in August, and they have since lost three games and settled for a stalemate once.

Bayern Munich form (all competitions):.

FC Koln form (all competitions):.

Bayern's injuries are still extensive despite the break from football, with left-back Alphonso Davies (hamstring) and goalkeeper Manuel Neuer (foot), as well as attackers Luis Diaz (hamstring) and Serge Gnabry (hamstring), among those to miss out.

Jonas Urbig will feature between the posts, while Josip Stanisic is almost certain to be stationed at left-back, with Dayot Upamecano and Jonathan Tah set to start as centre-backs.

In the forward line, Ballon d'or-winner Harry Kane may play ahead of a supporting cast consisting of Lennart Karl, Michael Olise and Nathaniel Brown.

Koln are also dealing with several injury problems, especially in defence considering both Timo Hubers and Rav van den Berg will be absent.

Joel Schmied, Jahmai Simpson-Pusey and Tom Krauss are the likely trio to start in the visitors' back three, while the club's attacking efforts will be led by forwards Marius Bulter and Said El Mala.

Bayern Munich possible starting lineup:.

Urbig; Laimer, Upamecano, Tah, Stanisic; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Karl, Olise, Brown; Kane.

FC Koln possible starting lineup:.

Schwabe; Schmied, Simpson-Pusey, Krauss; Sebulonsen, Maina, Okon-Engstler, Johannesson, Sosa; Bulter, El Mala.

Bayern Munich have shown that they are far from flawless at the back in recent months, so there should be openings for Koln.

However, the Bavarians have continued to be irresistible in attack despite their injuries, and they should be able to get the better of the visitors.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 18 Nov 2026 13:25.

Manchester United have reportedly set aside funds to sign Monaco striker Folarin Balogun during the January transfer window.

The 25-year-old was one of the standout performers for the USA at the 2026 World Cup and was heavily linked with a move to Tottenham Hotspur during the summer window.

Balogun also came close to joining Everton for £40m in the summer, but the proposed move collapsed after he failed a medical in the closing stages of negotiations.

A potential January departure could now be on the cards, with Man Utd reportedly keen to bring the striker to Old Trafford.

Arresting the club's rapid decline should be Mauricio Pochettino's first priority, but the manager would also be keen to bring in players of his choosing in January to strengthen key areas of the squad.

Having coached Balogun at international level, the prospect of a reunion is an obvious one, while the striker's representatives are also actively exploring a potential switch from Monaco to Old Trafford.

According to Football Insider, signing a new striker is Manchester United's second priority, with Pochettino keen to strengthen other areas of the pitch first.

The Red Devils want to reinforce their defence before turning their attention to the attack, although they could pursue Balogun if funds remain available after addressing their defensive shortcomings.

Monaco are reportedly willing to offload Balogun, who has managed just one Ligue 1 goal in six appearances this season, all of which have come from the bench.

The former Arsenal striker has scored 32 goals in 98 appearances for Monaco across all competitions and could prove a smart addition for Man Utd.

The Red Devils, however, could face stiff competition from Serie A giants Juventus, who are reportedly exploring a potential swap deal involving Edon Zhegrova.

Balogun is noted to be attracted by the prospect of moving to Turin, meaning United could face a significant battle for his signature if they are serious about securing his services.

The decision not to send Jayden Bogle off in Leeds United’s win over Tottenham Hotspur has been supported by a Premier League panel.

Leeds defeated Spurs 1-0 at Elland Road on November 7 and the losing side felt the hosts should have been reduced to 10 men.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Marauding wing-back Bogle caught the back of the ankle of winger Mathys Tel, which forced the wideman out of action.

VAR (video assistant referee) did not call referee John Brooks over for another look and Bogle was not carded for the challenge at all.

The incident sparked plenty of controversy but Brooks’ call has been backed by the Premier League’s key match incidents panel.

According to recent reports, the panel said: “This was a split decision with the majority supporting the referee's on field call of no red card. The panel considered this to be a clear foul but the majority felt Bogle was looking to challenge with his right leg and his left leg came down on the back of Tel's ankle without the speed, force or intensity to be serious foul play.

“They felt that the contact made was very clearly reckless, but below the threshold for a red card. Two panellists felt that the challenge was sufficiently dangerous to merit a red card.

“The non-VAR intervention was also supported, 3:2, on the basis that the majority considered the challenge to be reckless, therefore not a clear and obvious error.”.

Spurs signalled their intention to appeal the decision and former Premier League referee Graham Barber felt Bogle should have been sent for an early bath.

Sources indicate that he said: “I thought it was a very, very poor challenge, it was reckless at best but you could describe it as dangerous and endangering the safety of the opponent, and did it endanger the safety of the opponent? Well, the answer is probably yes, because he had to leave the field of play about five minutes later.”.

  • That was the word Michael Duff used to describe Wayne Rooney's contribution to football this week.
  • Because one of the great players of his generation, England's most capped outfielder and top goalscorer until Harry Kane took both records, has spoken about considering taking his own life when at the peak of career with Manchester United.
  • Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

That was the word Michael Duff used to describe Wayne Rooney's contribution to football this week.

Because one of the great players of his generation, England's most capped outfielder and top goalscorer until Harry Kane took both records, has spoken about considering taking his own life when at the peak of career with Manchester United.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Recent findings suggest that some seem to think that the obscene amounts players of Rooney's profile get paid makes them immune to psychological problems, insulated against off-field concerns and fair game for any criticism going. That argument even seems to extend down the pyramid to those not earning small fortunes, but still lucky enough to be earning a living in a game many of us would have dearly loved to be paid to play.

Even when 48-year-old Duff was a player, in the Premier League with Burnley and at international level with Northern Ireland, that lack of empathy towards players dealing with personal or even physical issues was rife in the game as well as outside of it.

But now Rooney has gone public, Duff can tell the players now under his charge, at League One Bradford City, they should not suffer in shamed silence.

“I think we just see a superstar earning £300,000 a week or whatever he's earning and you think it must be all right for him,” says former Barnsley and Huddersfield Town manager Duff.

“I can assure you none of our lads are earning £300,000 a week but they've all got their own lives as well.

“There's a lot more exposure now, with social media and things – they're all on it.

“That's why I say it is a tough life.

Sources indicate that “You have to give up a lot and it's easy to fall into (depression) particularly when you are injured, a long-term one, and you see all your mates going out onto the training pitch. It's all you want to do.

“So we have to help players and educate them.”.

Duff thinks Rooney's admission – albeit long after he retired – can help to educate those within the game.

“I played with Clarke Carlisle (at Burnley), who tried to kill himself,” recalls Duff. “You look back and you think I probably should have spotted something there.

“But it was all banter or 'The state of him,' that sort of thing.

“It was probably a cry for help but you didn't know at the time because you weren't educated.

“So for someone at that level to come out and say that about the height of his fame playing at the top, top, top level...

“That's sort of almost like the release is the football pitch. They just want to play football because that's where they're at the happiest.

Recent findings suggest that “So I think it's really good what he's done. I think it's notable with the education.”.

And it is not just the approach to mental complications where Duff sees a vast improvement when it comes to the well-being of footballers.

“In the old days, it was just 'Get on with it' – injuries and concussions, all those sort of things,” he argues.

“The manager would tell the doctor, 'He ain't coming off' and the player's like, 'I ain't coming off.'.

“It's irrelevant what the player thinks any more. It's the safeguarding of the players. It is really notable.”.

And social media can be a release for the jealousy of others with footballers in their sights.

It has been revealed that “Part of the job is you get a stick and abuse,” acknowledges Duff. “Sometimes it goes too far.

Recent findings suggest that “Everyone's got an opinion but you're not allowed to have one back (as a footballer). They are human beings.

In a recent development, “I don't go on social media. I don't need to. If we win, someone will say good things, if we don't, they won't.

“But it's when it starts getting personal it's a slightly different thing.

“And there's other pressures that people don't see.

In a recent development, “They see putting a shirt on and playing in front of 20,000, which is amazing but there's loads of other pressures within that. Whether it's money or whether it's providing for a family or looking after an ill parent or something like that.”.

What brought Duff onto the topic of mental health in football was a first serious injury of his career for 22-year-old Bantams forward Bobby Pointon, who is not expected to play again in 2026 because of a knee problem.

Where once you would hear stories of even managerial greats refusing to even acknowledge the presence of injured players at the training ground, now football is super-focused on looking after them mentally.

According to recent reports, “Hopefully it's not as bad as what we think,” comments Duff. “But we're in that sort of don't-know situation at the minute.

“It's his first (serious injury) so part of his education is learning what to do, how to live when you're injured.

“We need to help him and educate him to get through these periods because he just wants to play football.

“It underlines the importance of the topic.”.

Voyager 1 achieves a cosmic first: one ‘light day’ from Earth

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (809 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft (artist’s illustration) is still sailing through space even as its power supply fails.Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech.
  • In a recent development, A spacecraft has set a profound cosmic record.
  • Voyager 2 enters interstellar space after 41 years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft (artist’s illustration) is still sailing through space even as its power supply fails.Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech.

In a recent development, A spacecraft has set a profound cosmic record. At 5.16 a.m. EST on 18 November, NASA’s Voyager 1 reached a distance of one light day, or 25.9 billion kilometres, from Earth — farther than any object made by humans has gone before. That means it is now so far away that a signal travelling at light speed from Earth’s surface will take at least a full 24 hours to reach the trailblazing spacecraft.

Voyager 2 enters interstellar space after 41 years.

Voyager 2 enters interstellar space after 41 years.

The probe has been flying away from Earth for more than 49 years. “It has taken longer than half of a typical human lifespan to reach that distance — so on that level it’s amazing,” says Deana Weibel, an anthropologist at Grand Valley State University in Allendale, Michigan, who studies space exploration. At the same time, she notes, Voyager 1 is only a fraction of the distance towards the star closest to the Solar System: Proxima Centauri, which is 4.2 light years (almost 1.3 parsecs, or more than 1,500 light days) away.

Industry observers note that voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, rolled out from Earth in 1977 to explore the outer Solar System. Both passed out of the heliosphere — the realm in which the Sun protects Earth and other bodies from the influence of deep space — years ago, and are now hurtling through interstellar space, where they are experiencing frigid temperatures nearing –80 ºC. Their plutonium power is dwindling, and mission controllers are having to turn off scientific instruments on the probes to conserve as much power as possible. Voyager 1 is expected to lose communications with Earth in 2029 and its twin will do so in 2031, when their power finally dies.

Until then, they continue to do science with the few instruments left — sending back the only direct observations of interstellar space that have ever been made. Every day, the Voyagers are measuring what happens in the space between stars, including the surprising effects of storms of particles streaming outwards from the Sun.

Between 1979 and 1989, the Voyagers reshaped scientific understanding of the Solar System as they flew past Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Their discoveries include volcanoes on Jupiter’s moon Io — the first volcanism known beyond Earth — and a crackly water-ice crust on Jupiter’s moon Europa that is now thought to hide a potentially life-friendly ocean beneath it.

In a recent development, voyager 1 travels faster than Voyager 2 and exited the heliosphere in 2012 (see ‘Leaving it all behind’). Voyager 2 followed six years later.

Even though they are now in interstellar space, the spacecraft continue to measure changes wrought by the Sun. They discovered how blasts of solar material sometimes make it all the way through the heliosphere to produce shockwaves in the otherwise quiet interstellar realm. The Voyagers have observed these disturbances as changes in magnetic fields, energetic particles and other environmental variables that they measure. Starting around 2020, for instance, an incoming pressure front caused magnetic fields around the Voyagers to increase drastically, then drop six years later. Researchers are working to find out why that is.

“I think people didn’t quite anticipate how far out these influences could be felt,” notes Jamie Rankin, a space physicist at Princeton University in Newly introduced Jersey and the Voyagers’ deputy project scientist. That suggests that stars beyond the Sun might also be influencing the interstellar medium more than was previously thought, Rankin says — “so that’s where it gets fun”.

Barnsley FC try to strengthen their hand with olive branch to fans but Sheffield Wednesday's derby woes could be their best bet

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Reds have tried to strengthen their hand by agreeing to meet with unhappy supporters but the biggest thing in their favour at Oakwell could be doubts in the minds of the visitors.
  • For a first League One away game as Owls manager, Dave Challinor would surely like to face a team as down in the dumps as Barnsley.
  • Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Reds have tried to strengthen their hand by agreeing to meet with unhappy supporters but the biggest thing in their favour at Oakwell could be doubts in the minds of the visitors.

For a first League One away game as Owls manager, Dave Challinor would surely like to face a team as down in the dumps as Barnsley.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Only kept off the bottom by Bromley's woeful goal difference, Daniel Stendel's side have not won in the league since September 2, nine matches ago.

Consecutive cup wins in which they put 14 goals past lower-division opposition feel like a mirage after they were put back in their box by Wigan Athletic. Captain Cameron McGeehan was booked, and is suspended for Friday's home game.

With a pre-match protest planned, chairman Neerav Parekh will meet independent supporters groups and the media to try to address the disquiet, but not until Friday December 4, with a wider fans’ forum to follow.

So it all points one way, until you consider the geography.

Because derbies can be great levellers, and more importantly the Owls have a hang-up against opponents from Yorkshire.

In their last 14 such matches, their only victory was a 2-1 win over Middlesbrough on Easter Monday 2025, when Anthony Musaba scored an 89th-minute winner.

Much of the squad played no part in many of those defeats, and last season's matches against Boro, Hull City and Sheffield United can be written off, so handicapped were the Owls.

But the pattern has continued this season in a division they are expected to be strong in.

Bradford City inflicted their first defeat back in League One with an August 1-0 win which flattered the beaten hosts.

And points dropped against Huddersfield Town and Doncaster Rovers were nails in manager Henrik Pedersen's coffin.

It took a late fightback and a Terriers implosion for Wednesday to escape with a 2-2 draw from a game Martin Drury's side had much the better of for all but the last few minutes.

If that amplified doubts about Pedersen's management, Doncaster's third and at present last league win of the campaign, 2-0 at home to the Owls, confirmed them in the eyes of the board.

The angry away fans who chanted "You're getting sacked in the morning" were right.

It shows how psychological hurdles like this can outlive personnel changes on the field and in the dugout.

It should not have much bearing on Friday, but most probably will. And with four White Rose teams for company in League One, it is a bad division for any Yorkshire team to have a derby hang-up in.

On the more positive side, win in front of a packed away end which can be heard loud and clear in the tunnel and it will go a long way towards forging the bonds Challinor needs to make the most of Wednesday's biggest asset – their fanbase.

But if Barnsley can play on their derby insecurity, a home win would do wonders at the best time of the season to find some momentum.

Even for a derby, the stakes are high.

Sources indicate that in fact, the head coach Ruben Amorim has even deployed him as a wing-back on occasion. Given the injuries to Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze the Englishman’s role has become an even more key one than first imagined.

Hutchinson met with fans this afternoon at the Milan Store in San Babila in the city centre. While at the event, the winger gave an interview to the reporters who were present, with MilanNews relaying his words.

How have these first few months at Milan been? Are you raising your game?

“It’s going well, the coach is happy, but I think there’s still a lot to do. I’m earning myself some space… From here on out, we have to keep winning.”.

Industry observers note that we often see you on the wing. Do you prefer to play there or as a second striker?

Recent findings suggest that “Personally, I like to play anywhere, but preferably on the right flank. Then, wherever the coach puts me, I try to adapt, do my job, and perform to my best, following his tactical instructions. He knows what I can do with the ball. He simply tells me to create and give my all.”.

How is your relationship with Amorim?

“He talks to me about what to do with the ball and to do my best.”.

Why this difference in performance between Serie A and the Europa League?

“It’s hard to say… There have been games where we haven’t performed well due to silly mistakes, but I think we need to push forward from now on and get back on track for the Europa League. We have the right team to do it. We need to win and be at our best in every game.”.

What has struck you most about the fans in Italy these past months?

It has been revealed that “Definitely the passion surrounding the club. At the stadium, everyone is behind the team. It’s fantastic, I’ve never experienced anything like it before.”.

Do you think Milan can win the Scudetto?

“We’ve got the players, we have a good squad, and even though we’re still missing some leaders at times, I think we’re building on that. I think the coaches and the coaching staff are guiding us very well. Once everything clicks together perfectly, we’ll do great things.”.

Do you still see yourself at Milan in the coming seasons?

Industry observers note that “It’s my dream. After this season, I hope to be signed permanently. I see myself playing here for a long time to come.”.

What’s the feeling of playing in a historic stadium like San Siro?

“It’s crazy. The fans, even the away fans… It’s a unique feeling. It makes you want to give your all for the fans, create special moments, and win.”.

What are the differences between the Premier League and Serie A?

Sources indicate that “They’re both tough. When other teams play against Milan, they always want to give their all. They’re always tough matches. Tactically, it’s more defensive here.

Recent findings suggest that “In the Premier League, you probably have more space and the quality is probably a little higher, but Serie A is a tough league. There’s not that big a difference, there’s not that big a gap.”.

Is there any team-mate you’ve grown close to?

In a recent development, “No, I have a good relationship with everyone. They’ve all welcomed me very well, and obviously it’s easier with the guys who speak English.”.

Do you dream of making the national team?

“I’m trying to focus on my club. I want to perform well for Milan and then we’ll see.”.

By Saikat Mandal | 18 Nov 2026 14:28.

Manchester United and Manchester City are reportedly showing keen interest in signing Bayern Munich sensation Leonard Prescott.

The 17-year-old is a highly-rated young goalkeeper who has progressed through Bayern's youth ranks, but several clubs are now monitoring his situation.

Arsenal have reportedly been tracking the youngster, while contract talks with Bayern have not progressed as hoped.

Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur and Italian giants Juventus have also made contact over a potential move for Prescott, whose current contract is due to expire next summer.

According to TeamTalk, Manchester United and Manchester City have also joined the race for his signature and made contact with Prescott's representatives.

There are suggestions that the teenager could potentially develop into the best goalkeeper in Europe in his age group.

A move away from Bayern is now a genuine possibility, although the German champions could still convince the highly-rated youngster to commit his long-term future to the Allianz Arena.

Prescott does not turn 18 until September, meaning he would be unable to move to England before 2028.

There is a growing feeling that the current season could be Manuel Neuer's last at the club.

Jonas Urbig has proved to be an able deputy, and the German goalkeeper is expected to take over as Bayern's first choice once Neuer hangs up his gloves.

Prescott therefore faces an uphill battle to establish himself, with Bayern reportedly considering the signing of another goalkeeper to serve as their number two next summer.

Bayern rate the teenager highly, but his representatives are not entirely convinced by the pathway being laid out for him at the Allianz Arena, offering encouragement to the interested Premier League clubs.

  • Thomas Tuchel hailed the 'best performance of my time as manager' after England beat world champions Spain in a crazy, brilliant see-sawing drama of a Nations League tie.
  • England played the best football of Tuchel's two-year reign as coach to end Spain's world record 43-match unbeaten run.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 18:10 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 19:58 EST, 15 November 2026.

Thomas Tuchel hailed the 'best performance of my time as manager' after England beat world champions Spain in a crazy, brilliant see-sawing drama of a Nations League tie.

England played the best football of Tuchel's two-year reign as coach to end Spain's world record 43-match unbeaten run.

England raced into a 3-0 lead with a penalty from Harry Kane, and further goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

But they played the last half an hour of the game with ten men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for pulling back Lamine Yamal.

Spain got two goals back to set up a nerve-wracking finish but goalkeeper James Trafford, in the team ahead of Jordan Pickford, pulled off a miracle double save in the dying minutes to seal the win.

'What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,' Tuchel said after the game. 'Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

Thomas Tuchel stated England's display in the win over Spain was the best in his time as boss.

It has been revealed that 'It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.

'It is the best performance of my time and they are unbeaten for 43 matches and that was a complete performance in that environment. To impose our identity on them was a real achievement.

According to recent reports, 'Declan Rice noted he knew we were going to win and I could feel the true belief. This was the moment we wanted to prove ourselves. You need to rely on your teammates. That is why I am very proud of the win.'.

Tuchel also questioned the decision to give Anderson a straight red, made by a referee he once labelled a 'one out of 10'.

The Man City midfielder was sent off because Clement Turpin adjudged him not to have been making an attempt to play the ball when he fouled Yamal.

'The red card and the penalty is always a big decision and I needed to understand why it was a double punishment but... OK,' Tuchel told ITV Sport.

'From then it was a long 30 minutes but I don't want to focus on that because there were so, so many positives.'.

He at the moment sits at the chief understudy to Harry Kane, who was recently crowned winner of the coveted Ballon d’Or award.

Hateley, who won 32 England caps between 1984 and 1992 and had a loan spell at Leeds in 1996, has rued the timing of Calvert-Lewin’s emergence on the international scene.

He told The Yorkshire Post via London.Bet: “I'm going to say the only way that Calvert-Lewin will get a game is if he's (Kane) injured, because I think he will be first in. He's got to play the long game. Harry's going to play for a long time, I think.

Recent findings suggest that “Sports science and everything going forward is all geared for playing longer. The way Harry lives his life, his lifestyle, his ability to adapt as a player... Calvert-Lewin is in the wrong place at the wrong time, wrong era.

In a recent development, “He's just got himself stuck behind an absolute legend of a player that just seems to get better and better and better. He'll (Kane) crush 150 plus games, the goal tally will go up and up and up. That's who you've just got to sit behind, but you've got to be ready.”.

Industry observers note that calvert-Lewin may not be England’s number nine but he is certainly the chief marksman at Elland Road. He has enjoyed a career rejuvenation in West Yorkshire, notching 20 goals across 51 appearances since his free transfer move from Everton in the summer of 2025.

Hateley noted: “You've got to be doing your stuff at Leeds, you've got to be scoring goals at Leeds, staying fit, playing well.

“I think the problem with Calvert-Lewin is, in his younger career, there was a lot of niggly injuries. A lot of setbacks, holding him back, not being able to get on runs.

“When you're being selected for an international set-up, you have to be consistently on top of your game. You're persistently good. You're always there knocking at the door. That's what Calvert-Lewin's got to do now.

“He's got to keep himself fit. He's got to do good things with Leeds and score goals. It's as simple as that.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 15:06, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 15:07.

Real Madrid have announced that Arda Guler has signed a latest contract at Bernabeu until the end of the 2031-32 campaign.

The Turkey international made the move to Bernabeu from Fenerbahce in the summer of 2023, and he has represented the capital giants on 126 occasions, scoring 22 goals and registering 32 assists in the process.

Guler has started the campaign with four goals and seven assists in 14 appearances in all competitions, including three goals and five assists in 12 La Liga outings.

Real Madrid have revealed that the 21-year-old has agreed a fresh deal in the Spanish capital until the summer of 2032.

In a recent development, "Real Madrid C. F. and Arda Guler have agreed to extend the contract of our player, who will remain linked to the club until June 30, 2032," read a statement from the capital giants.

Guler has started 10 of Real Madrid's 12 La Liga matches this season, demonstrating his importance for Los Blancos, although he has only played in two of their four Champions League league stage fixtures this term.

The playmaker missed the team's 2026-27 European opener against Inter Milan through suspension, while he was rested against AEK Athens in their last game in the competition.

Guler has not scored more than six times in a campaign for Real Madrid since his arrival, but he is already just two goals off that total in November.

Real Madrid won La Liga and the Champions League during Guler's first campaign at the club, but he only featured on 12 occasions in 2023-24.

Guler has won five trophies during his time at Bernabeu, but this could be his best campaign yet both from a personal and team point of view.

Guler is expected to be in the starting team when Real Madrid continue their La Liga campaign against Celta Vigo on November 21.

The playmaker will then be hoping to make his third Champions League appearance of the season when Los Blancos face PSV Eindhoven in the competition on November 24.

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

According to recent reports, the three significant guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

Sources indicate that that was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the big three were on the difference was obvious.

“We had moments in the game in the first half … [when] we arrived in very dangerous positions,” Arteta said. “With a lot of advantage, our technical quality wasn’t good enough to deliver moments of real threat and especially to be able to sustain the attack, so we allowed certain transitions.” He said that he made some changes at half-time, as managers are wont to do, and that things improved but the real change was clear when he made the substitutions.

It has been revealed that “It was a joy to watch,” Arteta said. “The three goals were unbelievable, the connections, the timings, the quality they delivered to score. Three different players and a lot of players participating in those goals, so overall very, very happy.” He had played Myles Lewis-Skelly at left-back again to give Riccardo Calafiori a rest. Saka had been ill during the week and not in a position to start.

In the opposing technical area was Davide Ancelotti, the 37-year-old son of Carlo, with his father’s trademark slow amble to the edge of the technical area. Young Ancelotti had drilled his team well, but once they were exposed to the high-pace recovery and sharp passing geometry of the Arsenal substitutes there was to be no coming back. Saka made the second for Eberechi Eze who had started the game on the left and the Arsenal No 7 scored the third himself. The home fans sang again about being champions of England and they certainly looked the part.

According to recent reports, the Arsenal players wore black armbands to mark the passing, aged 94, of Ken Friar, the club’s life vice-president. He had served the club from 1945 to 2014 and was variously club secretary, managing director and a driving force in building the stadium in which they now play. Even Arteta, no sentimentalist, insisted on beginning his press conference with a tribute.

For Arteta’s players, there will be a much bigger test than this one in Munich next week against Bayern. Arsenal have already won in Naples but a victory at Bayern would be significant beyond that. Arsenal have won all but one of their 10 games this season – that major defeat at the Amex Stadium, almost one month ago. They clearly have another gear to go to when required although ideally, Arteta would not always have to ask it of the same players. The club have spent too much on this squad not to be able to trust the understudies.

Madueke did at least end the game with an assist. Of Saka’s understudy, Arteta said: “When you talk about players being clinical – what is clinical? Clinical sometimes means that they score one in every 500. It’s about generating volume and more actions and getting him into the good position because he will decide matches.”.

No goals for Gyokeres this season and a general acceptance that the time for persevering with him has passed. It could be ever-dwindling returns for him in terms of game-time as the season goes. He was a much better player than Gyokeres in an era when Arsenal were in decline.

A few things tactically: one adjustment attacking, one defending. But especially, that we had to increase the technical level. At this level, the teams are really well organised. We gave simple ball;s away, bad touches mistimed things. When we delivered the ball into the box it wasn’t the right area so we get caught, especially delivering from the right and [Lille] transition on the left.

The moment we started to do that better, we could counter-press, and start to play into the opposition’s box, and with the quality that we have we made a real difference there.

I had some moments in the first half but second half I had more. First touch was good, which was half the job, and then Noni [Madueke] was screaming “shoot” so I thought OK I have to shoot. And then yeah it went in nice.

According to recent reports, I wasn’t thinking too much. I saw the goal and thought I need to shoot. We needed that first goal, we were playing well just needed the goal. Happy to get that for the team.

Since returning to the competition under Arteta in 2023, they have won all 12 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals.

Including knock-out games, Arsenal have conceded just eight goals in 20 home matches, keeping 15 clean sheets.

Four of those goals came in effective dead rubbers against PSV in the 2025 last-16 (after Arsenal won 7-1 in Eindhoven) and against Kairat Almaty in the final game of last season’s league phase.

So in home Champions League games that matter, they have conceded just four goals in 18 matches: Serge Gnarby and Harry Kane for Bayern in the 2024 quarter-final, Ousmane Dembele in the 2025 semi-final and Lennart Karl for Bayern in last season’s league phase.

Will Olivier Giroud receive a warm welcome back to the Emirates Stadium? The Frenchman spent six years as an Arsenal player but burned a few bridges when he left the club for Chelsea, and then celebrated wildly when Chelsea beat Arsenal in the Europa League final of 2019. Now 40, Giroud has shown remarkable longevity and is unquestionably one of the best strikers of his generation. But can he hurt this formidable Arsenal defence? It’s a tough ask.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

In a recent development, as Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”.

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.
