After signing his new Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 18 Nov 2026 15:20.

Real Madrid defender Antonio Rudiger has debuted a passionate defence of Kylian Mbappe's contribution to the team, drawing a striking comparison with Cristiano Ronaldo, Karim Benzema and Gareth Bale to challenge criticism of the Frenchman's defensive work.

Mbappe has been one of Madrid's most prolific players since arriving from Paris Saint-Germain in 2024, reaching 100 goals for the Spanish giants despite their struggles to win major silverware over the past two seasons.

However, his extraordinary goalscoring record has not prevented questions being raised about his willingness to press opponents and contribute when Madrid are out of possession.

The glitch has become particularly prominent under Jose Mourinho, whose demanding approach requires his players to maintain their defensive organisation.

Rudiger believes some of those expectations are misplaced, arguing that a forward of Mbappe's quality should be judged primarily on his ability to decide matches.

Speaking in an exclusive interview with The Athletic, the former Chelsea centre-back questioned whether it made sense to demand the same defensive responsibilities from a player who has already delivered 100 goals for Madrid.

Sources indicate that "Should I tell Mbappe [...] to do my job? It makes no sense," Rudiger noted.

The German then pointed to one of the most successful attacking partnerships in Real Madrid's history to explain his position.

Rudiger believes Madrid's previous success offers an vital lesson about how to accommodate outstanding attacking players.

He recalled the celebrated partnership of Ronaldo, Bale and Benzema, who spearheaded the club's attack during a period that produced four Champions League titles between 2014 and 2018.

The trio were renowned for their individual attacking qualities and ability to deliver decisive moments in major matches.

Rudiger suggested that Madrid did not achieve those successes by constantly scrutinising their forwards' defensive contributions.

He pointed to the achievements of the three players before insisting that discussion of attackers should not always revolve around their work without the ball.

His argument is particularly relevant to Mbappe, whose goals have frequently provided Madrid with a decisive advantage even when the team's collective performances have attracted criticism.

The French international has continued to deliver exceptional numbers in front of goal, although Madrid have struggled to translate his individual productivity into the trophies expected at the Santiago Bernabeu.

According to recent reports, rudiger's comments do not suggest that Mbappe should be exempt from defensive responsibilities. Rather, the defender believes the rest of the team must find an effective balance around players whose greatest value comes in attacking positions.

The comparison with Ronaldo is especially significant given the Portuguese forward's standing at Madrid, where he scored 450 goals in 438 appearances and helped establish an era of sustained European dominance.

Mbappe has already been compared to Ronaldo following his spectacular individual performances for Madrid, but Rudiger has approached the comparison from a different perspective.

For the experienced defender, the question is how Madrid can create the conditions for their most influential attackers to flourish.

Rudiger also addressed another recurring criticism of Madrid's squad: the difficulty of managing a dressing room filled with established international stars.

The 33-year-old acknowledged that the club's collection of strong personalities can create challenges for any manager.

He referred to Rafael Benitez and Julen Lopetegui, whose spells in charge of Madrid ended prematurely, as examples of coaches who encountered similar difficulties.

"It's not a myth. That's the reality," Rudiger admitted when discussing the influence of massive personalities at the club.

His comments offer an insight into the environment Mourinho has inherited since returning to Madrid during the summer.

The Portuguese manager has been tasked with restoring the club's success after two seasons without a major trophy, with Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Junior among the players expected to lead that recovery.

Rudiger spoke positively about Mourinho's influence, revealing that the manager had contacted him towards the end of last season to explain his plans and express his desire to keep the German at the club.

He also described a lighter side to Mourinho's personality, explaining that the former Manchester United and Chelsea boss enjoys telling jokes in the dressing room while maintaining a far more demanding approach on the training pitch.

The defender extended his support to Vinicius, who has experienced a difficult start to the season and faced increased competition for his position.

Rudiger insisted that the Brazilian continues to work hard to improve his performances and remains an crucial figure in Madrid's looks.

Vinicius has recently rediscovered his goalscoring form with Brazil, scoring five times across two international friendlies against Japan and Singapore.

His return presents Mourinho with another selection decision as Madrid prepare to resume their domestic campaign.

For Rudiger, however, the responsibility for restoring Madrid's success cannot rest solely on the willingness of Mbappe, Vinicius or Bellingham to defend.

His comparison with Ronaldo's celebrated attacking partnership reflects a broader conviction that Madrid must find a collective structure capable of making the most of their attacking talent.

Mikael Silvestre has encouraged Manchester United to explore a move for Estevao – but doubts the forward could be coaxed to the Theatre of Dreams as he appears intent on ‘fighting for his place’ at Chelsea.

United spent in the region of £160million on upcoming signings in the summer, with club chiefs showing they were prepared to back Michael Carrick following an impressive third-place finish.

But any optimism that had grown amongst the fanbase in the back-end of last season rapidly faded as a 2-0 defeat away to Chelsea last month extended the Red Devils’ miserable winless run to nine matches in all competitions.

A stunning comeback victory over Roma followed by a 4-4 thriller at home to Aston Villa in the Premier League were ultimately not enough to save Carrick, who was relieved of his duties last Thursday.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach Mauricio Pochettino was subsequently announced as Carrick’s successor, with the Argentine officially vacating his position with the United States national team to start life in the role later this week.

Naturally, attentions have quickly turned towards the January transfer window, when United will be expected to splash the cash in the hope of boosting their prospects for the second half of the campaign.

United chiefs are set to resurrect their pursuit of a left-back as a priority to provide support for Luke Shaw after missing out on Newcastle’s Lewis Hall in the summer.

It’s understood the Old Trafford giants will also be in the market for attacking reinforcements on the back of a desperately disappointing start to the season for the likes of Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko.

According to Silvestre, Chelsea winger Estevao could represent a ‘good signing’ for United, with the Brazilian having made just one start in the Premier League under Xabi Alonso.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

That start happened to come against United, though, and the 19-year-old was widely praised for his performance as goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer proved decisive at Stamford Bridge.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

‘Well, Estevao played against United for Chelsea, and I think he’s shown why he should feature more,’ Silvestre told Betarades.gr.

‘It looks like he’s going to fight for his place in the team, so I don’t anticipate United making a move for him.

‘But he’s a good player for sure. He’s playing for the national team of Brazil, and I like his style. If he were available, he would be a good signing for United.’.

Asked why Newcastle and England star Hall may ‘make sense’ for United at left-back, Silvestre replied: ‘Lewis Hall had an impressive season with Newcastle, and he’s been on the club’s radar for sure.

‘The club made an attempt to sign him and other fullbacks, but couldn’t get it done.

‘They now have to rely on Luke Shaw, Diego Dalot, on Noussair Mazraoui, and on Patrick Dorgu, who has also been injured for quite some time. So that’s not been helpful either.’.

Another high-profile name heavily linked with United in recent weeks has been Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who has scored five goals in his opening nine appearances for Leeds this term.

But Silvestre, who won five Premier League titles with the Red Devils, believes the England striker would only be brought in as a stop-gap for his former club up front.

‘I think Dominic Calvert-Lewin would be a stop-gap,’ the ex-United and France defender explained.

‘I don’t think it’s a long-term. He doesn’t belong in a Manchester United squad. So I don’t know where this is coming from.

‘Yes, you need to have a look around for strikers because of the Sesko situation with his injury, and we are short in that department, but I wouldn’t consider Calvert-Lewin as an option.’.

All eyes will be on Anfield on Sunday when Pochettino takes charge of United for the first time against bitter rivals Liverpool.

Pochettino takes over the reins from Carrick with the club languishing down in 18th place in the Premier League, just point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace.

Mauricio Pochettino has spoken for the first time after officially starting work as Manchester United manager.

Pochettino was announced as the latest Man United head coach last week, replacing Michael Carrick, but his arrival at Carrington had been delayed due to finishing up with the United States Men’s National Team [USMNT].

The Argentine bowed out of international management by overseeing a 2-0 win for USA against Haiti in the early hours on Wednesday.

After fulfilling his post-match media obligations, Pochettino flew directly from Cincinnati to the UK, touching down at Manchester airport before midday and then travelling to Carrington.

November 18 was always intended to be the 54-year-old’s start date and in his first interview in Man Utd colours, Pochettino noted: “Very excited to be here, it's an honour, it's a privilege to be in this amazing club.

"Looking forward to starting work.".

"Mauricio Pochettino has officially started work as Manchester United head coach, marking the start of a dream role for the Argentinian," a club statement reads.

"Pochettino’s appointment was announced last Friday with an agreement he’ll begin on 18 November, once he had fulfilled his duties with the US Men’s National Team.

"As Mauricio explained during a press conference last week, it was crucial for him to maintain complete focus on two remaining fixtures with USMNT.

Sources indicate that "Pochettino oversaw two excellent wins over Haiti in the CONCACAF quarter finals. He then boarded a direct flight from Cincinnati to Manchester on Wednesday morning.

"Eager to get started, the 54-year-old travelled straight to Carrington to tour our training complex, meet a selection of players and staff, and begin work as our newly introduced head coach.".

All the better to eat you with: vampire bats (such as this common vampire bat, Desmodus rotundus) have an array of genetic adaptations that allow them to subsist on blood.Credit: Joel Sartore/Photo Ark/Nature Picture Library.

An analysis of vampire bats is offering clues as to how the animals sustain themselves on blood alone. Researchers found that the stomachs of all three vampire-bat species act as a stretchy, pH-neutral storage sac lined with thick layers of connective tissue that help it to balloon after a feast. These ‘stomachs’ contain high levels of fluid-transporting channels that help to shed excess water so the bats can fly home. Genes that encode metabolic pathways that convert blood proteins into fats and sugars are also upregulated in vampire bats, compared with non-vampire species.

Reference: bioRxiv preprint (not peer reviewed).

In a recent development, A genetic variant that seems to reduce the size of human brain areas involved in visual processing was inherited from Neanderthals. Scraps of Neanderthal DNA have been found in the genomes of many modern humans, but this variant seems to have an unusually powerful effect on brain anatomy, and people who carry the variant also have a reduced risk of schizophrenia. “Its effect is really one of the most beautiful and strong that I’ve ever seen,” says computational biologist Davide Marnetto.

Reference: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA paper.

A make-believe buddy can offer children comfort and encouragement when needed, and give them a way to practise dealing with conflict, she writes. The book is “a deeply researched and highly entertaining look at the world of imaginary companions”, writes science journalist Josie Glausiusz in her review, who fondly recalls her own two childhood imaginary friends — the inventively named Boy and Girl.

Industry observers note that the rules that were developed to explore Antarctica without disrupting its ecosystem could be a useful starting point for exploring worlds such as Jupiter’s icy moon Europa, argues astrobiologist Emma Johanna Puranen. (Nature Astronomy | 15 min read).

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The footballing world was rocked earlier this month as it was revealed that De Miguel had tragically passed away at the age of 30 after he was involved in a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Owono.
  • Owono had raced out of goal in the closing stages of the Spanish second-tier contest before clattering into De Miguel, whose severe head and chest injuries caused him to go into cardiac arrest.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andorra owner Gerard Pique says Jesus Owono ‘does not deserve’ the 12-game suspension he received following the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

The footballing world was rocked earlier this month as it was revealed that De Miguel had tragically passed away at the age of 30 after he was involved in a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Owono.

Owono had raced out of goal in the closing stages of the Spanish second-tier contest before clattering into De Miguel, whose severe head and chest injuries caused him to go into cardiac arrest.

It swiftly became apparent that De Miguel required urgent medical attention and while the centre-forward’s condition was described as ‘stable but serious’ after he was carried from the field and taken to hospital, his condition quickly deteriorated – and he died the following day.

Players and organisations have united in support of De Miguel’s friends and family in the days and weeks that have followed, with heartfelt tributes shared and moments of silence observed across the globe.

Last week, Owono learned that he would be banned for Andorra’s next 12 matches for the role he played in the deadly collision, with the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee stating that the player had ‘violently struck an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’.

It went on: ‘The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge.

The statement added that the ‘nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances’ meant that the ‘maximum sanction’ was ‘justified’.

It was also confirmed that the match involving Andorra and Tenerife – which was called off when the teams were locked at 2-2 deep into stoppage time – would not be replayed.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘This avoids having to resume play from the precise moment at which the tragic incident occurred,’ it read.

Owono’s suspension has received a mixed reaction in Spain, with some feeling it too lenient while others have called for the ‘distressed’ goalkeeper to be given greater support.

According to Andorra owner Pique, the former Barcelona, Manchester United and Spain defender, Owono is ‘not to blame’ for the tragic outcome of the deadly collision.

‘I truly believe that imposing the maximum sanction on Jesus for this action puts him in a situation he does not deserve,’ he noted in a statement.

‘He is not to blame for all of this having happened.’.

Pique pointed to a separate incident earlier this month in Spanish football, when Albacete attacker Jose Corpas accidentally kicked Sabadell’s Quadri Liameed in the head during a second-tier encounter.

‘Fortunately Quadri is fine, the consequences in this case were not fatal, and the committee decided to sanction Corpas with three matches,’ Pique added.

‘With all this, my reflection is: what is being sanctioned, the action or the consequences?’.

Pique, a World Cup winner with Spain in 2010, made it clear that Owono would likely require a significant break away from the game before being able to compete again.

‘Jesus is going to need far more than 12 matches before he is available and able to play,’ he continued.

‘No sanction is going to bring De Miguel back to us.’.

Tenerife’s grieving squad returned to action for the first time since De Miguel’s death against Cueta on Sunday.

Goals from Nacho Gil and Neal Viereck sealed Tenerife a 2-0 victory on an emotional day the club’s Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ashley Young believes Manchester United will continue to struggle until the club changes the way it is run, while he is also unsure whether Mauricio Pochettino will have enough time to implement his ideas.

United revealed the appointment of Pochettino on a two-and-a-half-year deal to succeed Michael Carrick this week, with the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss set to take his first training session on Thursday.

Pochettino becomes the fourth permanent manager to take the reins at Old Trafford since INEOS and Sir Jim Ratcliffe bought a minority stake and took over the day-to-day running of United in February 2024.

Upon buying a 27.5 per cent stake in the club, Ratcliffe insisted United needed to put a stop to the managerial turnover that had become commonplace since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013.

Yet just over two-and-a-half years on, nothing has changed, with Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Carrick all being shown the door.

Pochettino has a huge task on his hands, with United currently sitting in the relegation zone, and Young believes that even if results initially improve, significant change won’t occur until changes are made in the boardroom.

“This season has been tough. I've stated that Michael Carrick worked miracles last season with the squad that was there,” Young tells Standard Sport.

“Do I think things still need to change? Yeah, I think until things change from the top down to the manager, (United will continue to struggle). I think that things might start well, but there's always going to be some issues there.”.

Pochettino has been on United’s radar for several years, and he came close to taking the head coach role on a number of occasions over the last decade before eventually agreeing to take over from Carrick.

Revered for his time in charge of Tottenham between 2014 and 2019, Pochettino has since struggled to replicate the same success he enjoyed in north London, and he leaves the US men’s national team having met rather than exceeded expectations at the World Cup this summer.

Man Utd confirm FIVE exits as Pochettino overhaul begins.

Pochettino ‘very excited’ as first words as Man Utd manager revealed.

United will be aware they are not appointing the same Pochettino they courted in 2016, when the Argentine was heavily linked with the role after Louis van Gaal’s departure, and have therefore handed him a short-term deal.

This season has been tough. I've said that Michael Carrick worked miracles last season with the squad that was there.

Young, though, is not sure whether Pochettino will have enough time to instil his ideas and stabilise the club after a disastrous start to the season.

“I think Mauricio Pochettino has probably gone in and said that he wants reassurances that he's going to get the players in and get the players out that he needs,” Young continued.

“But if you look at, especially when he was at Tottenham, it took him two or three years to rebuild that side. He got players in that were hungry, that wanted to play for him.

“I think if you talk to players that have played for him, it's going to be tough, it's going to be hard. So I think there's going to be a rebuild there.

“But also, he's been given a two-and-a-half-year contract. At Tottenham, it was three years to rebuild the team.

“So I think that's interesting in itself. Hopefully things can go better and go well, and the club can be stabilised. But I still think that something needs to change at the top.”.

Young was speaking ahead of the launch of the Panini Official EFL Sticker Collection and remarked his first memories of collecting the stickers came as a kid at school.

“I always mentioned that, you know, when you used to open packs and get a shiny (sticker), it was the best feeling ever. It was like Christmas come all over again.

In a recent development, “First memories of swapping at school as well. Kids at break time were like, ‘have you got this, have you got that?’ Trying to get the best ones.”.

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:11 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 21:21 EST, 15 November 2026.

Tenerife have returned to action for the first time since Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel was tragically killed in a collision during a game with FC Andorra earlier this month.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono came flying out of his goal and wiped out De Miguel with a high challenge, which resulted in the striker being admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

Thirteen days on from the incident, Tenerife played their first game since the player's death as they took on AD Ceuta CF in LaLiga Hypermotion action – with the game filled with tributes to the star.

Players gave a floral tribute as they arrived for the match, and gathered outside gate nine of the Heliodoro Rodríguez Lopez Stadium – the shirt number he wore.

Grief-stricken Tenerife stars, meanwhile, took to the field carrying a bouquet of flowers, and placed it at the scene of the incident.

Both sets of players and fans then observed a minute's silence in memory of De Miguel before the game kicked off.

🕊️❤️ THE NINTH MINUTE BELONGED TO JESÚS DE MIGUEL! 🥹🏟️ Football took a back seat during Tenerife's first match following his passing.👏 In the ninth minute, the stadium came together in a heartfelt tribute to honor his memory.💔 Some losses are felt far beyond the pitch.… pic.twitter.com/mqPy4aE9Q3.

CF Tenerife returned to action for the first time since the death of Jesus de Miguel in a game flooded with tributes.

Both sets of players gathered around the centre circle before the game to pay tribute.

The forward (pictured in 2025) passed away after being on the receiving end of a brutal tackle.

The game was then brought to a pause in the ninth minute, so the players could pay another tribute.

Fans inside the stadium unveiled a tifo which read: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternal blanquiazul', which translates to: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally white and blue.'.

Other fans held up white and blue cards beside the tifo, with others in the ground applauding. When Tenerife scored, De Miguel's shirt was held in the air.

After the game, which Tenerife won 2-0, both teams gathered in the centre circle to place De Miguel's shirt on a bouquet of flowers, and the fans applauded to bring an end to an emotional day.

The tragedy occurred as the game against Andorra entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Industry observers note that owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture. Fans have chanted 'murderer' in his direction.

Before the game, players gathered outside gate nine - the shirt numebr de Miguel wore.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been handed a 12-match ban and may never play football again.

On Friday, the goalkeeper was hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

His manager Carles Manso has stated: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that (he will do so).'.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Antonio Conte believes "sooner of later the circle will close" on his time at Juventus as he hinted at a possible return to the Bianconeri in the future.

Conte is right now out of work after agreeing to terminate his contract with Napoli a year early following the 2025-26 season, when they finished second to champions Inter.

The 57-year-old led the Partenopei to their fourth Serie A title a year earlier, while it was only their second Scudetto in the post-Diego Maradona era.

His 62% win rate in Serie A with Napoli is the third highest of all Partenopei coaches, behind only Maurizio Sarri (69%) and Luciano Spalletti (68%).

Conte had been linked with a return to the Italy national team after their failure to reach a third successive World Cup, with Manchester United also seen as a possible destination before the Red Devils chose to appoint Mauricio Pochettino last week.

But Conte enjoyed most of his success, both as a player and as a head coach, with Juventus, where he spent a decade representing the club on the pitch.

He was appointed as Luigi Delneri's successor in May 2011 and went on to win three successive Serie A titles, along with the Supercoppa Italiana in 2012 and 2013.

Turin remains the only stop in his coaching career where he has lasted longer than two years, and he believes unfinished business will eventually draw him back.

"I think that sooner or later the circle will close," Conte confessed in an interview with Cronache di Spogliatoio, which was teased on Wednesday.

"I know I left something behind, and I know that eventually the circle will be closed with Juventus.

"There have been moments in the past where we could have reunited, but it's been difficult because two things have to align.

"I have to be available and Juventus have to be looking for a coach who isn't currently employed.".

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) November 14, 2026.

Conte explained that two recent vacancies in Turin slipped away because of timing, pushing him toward Serie A rivals Inter in 2019.

He also revealed he had been on the verge of becoming head coach of Juventus in 2009 just before leaving Bari.

But a disagreement over the use of Brazilian playmaker Diego saw the deal collapse, and he would go on to join Atalanta.

Recent findings suggest that "There have been two instances. Once, when Juventus decided to hire Maurizio Sarri, I was available and later ended up at Inter," Conte added.

Recent findings suggest that "Then there was a second time when I was free, just as Giuntoli arrived. Giuntoli decided to go for Motta and I went to Napoli.

In a recent development, "I went, walking in as the Juve manager and then we started talking. They asked me how I wanted to play, and I replied with a '4-2-4'. They remarked 'but where would you play Diego?'.

"I answered 'you were the ones who signed him, even though I remarked that we already have four forwards. So I would play him alongside one of the strikers'.

It has been revealed that "Then they told me 'well, Diego wants to play in a 4-3-1-2'. Imagine my anger at the time. Although, that anger demonstrates that I'm a direct person who doesn't make compromises.

"Anyone else, literally anyone else, would have said 'sure, I'll even play him in goal if you want, just let me sign the contract and I’ll join Juve'.

"I stood firm in my ideas, firm in my convictions, and firm in the fact that I wasn't going to make any compromises or promise anything I knew I wouldn't deliver.

"So, I told them 'if a player decides how we play, then I’m not the right coach for you'. And that was it. I walked away and by the time I left that meeting.".

The Portuguese had an outstanding 2025-26 Premier League season, scoring nine goals and registering 21 assists in 35 appearances, while he has six goals and three assists in 14 appearances for the Red Devils this term.

Fernandes has struggled to show his best form for much of the campaign, though, and a departure next year is seen as possible.

Young, who played for Man United between 2011 and 2020, has urged the 20-time English champions to make a move for Forest's Gibbs-White.

The 26-year-old has scored 37 goals and registered 38 assists in 180 matches for Forest in all competitions, including one goal and three assists in nine Premier League outings this term.

According to recent reports, “Bruno has been fantastic for Manchester United. He has been, and no one can say that he hasn’t,” Young told Standard Sport.

Industry observers note that “There's obviously been a few things that have come up of late. If a club like Manchester United are going to build a team around him, he's going to be 33 next year.

“If it was me, I would be looking at going to get another number 10 and build it around him. I'd go and get Morgan Gibbs-White. I think he's got 18 months left on his contract.

According to recent reports, "He's established in the Premier League, he’s a leader, he's showing his qualities at Nottingham Forest. And I'm sure Nottingham Forest won't thank me for saying that.”.

Gibbs-White has long been linked with a move away from Forest, but he signed a newly introduced deal with the club in the summer of 2025 after a proposed switch to Tottenham Hotspur failed to materialise.

The Englishman is surely in line for a move to an elite club in the not too distant future, and he would be an ideal signing for Man United given his skill set and Premier League experience.

Industry observers note that ‘I’d keep Bruno [Fernandes], I’d keep Kobbie [Mainoo], I’d keep [Youri] Tielemans, Mount would have to go, [Andrey] Santos… Mauricio may like him because he’s young, quite mobile, he’s aggressive, he might get something out of him. More than just a football club: Cardinale’s vision to make AC Milan a multi-billion empire

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1843 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In case you weren’t aware from his repeatedly bold comments in the media, Gerry Cardinale has big plans for AC Milan.
  • The RedBird Capital founder and chief has made one concept very clear: while he is at the helm, Milan are no longer just a football club, but a platform that aims to integrate sports, infrastructure, and entertainment.
  • Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In case you weren’t aware from his repeatedly bold comments in the media, Gerry Cardinale has big plans for AC Milan.

The RedBird Capital founder and chief has made one concept very clear: while he is at the helm, Milan are no longer just a football club, but a platform that aims to integrate sports, infrastructure, and entertainment. Of course AC Milan will be at the centre of the web, but the idea is to expand.

Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The proof of this comes from a three-letter acronym: MSE. It stands for Milan Sports & Entertainment and it is the new holding company created by RedBird. The idea, simply put, is to bring together investments and activities in various sectors under one umbrella.

Sources indicate that as La Gazzetta dello Sport recall, Cardinale explained to the Financial Times that the assets involved could be valued in the mid-single-digit billions, meaning several billion dollars. So, how does he plan to get there?

Cardinale linked the creation of MSE to the process initiated with the acquisition of Milan: “Milan Sports & Entertainment is the culmination of this work and of what we have built since we first invested in the club four years ago.”.

In his interview with La Gazzetta, Cardinale clarified that the new structure is also created to support the Rossoneri’s sporting ambitions: “The driving force behind operations like this is to provide Milan with the financial strength needed to compete in the transfer market and secure the best players in the world.”.

In a recent development, there are examples of this kind of model working already. Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, AEG and Fenway Sports Group are among the most prominent and – given his background in the USA – Cardinale knows each of them well.

According to CNBC valuations, KSE was worth $26.05bn in 2026, FSG $15.37bn, and AEG $11.99bn in 2025, excluding music and hotel businesses.

KSE boasts franchises such as the Los Angeles Rams, Denver Nuggets, Colorado Avalanche and Arsenal, as well as venues such as SoFi Stadium, Ball Arena, and Emirates Stadium. The group combines sports, infrastructure and real estate development such as Hollywood Park, the district built around SoFi Stadium.

AEG – founded by Philip Anschutz – have instead built its model on the management and development of venues. It owns or manages venues such as Crypto.com Arena and The O2 in London plus the Los Angeles Kings and LA Galaxy, and operates in concert promotion and ticketing. The LA LIVE project developed around Crypto.com Arena puts the venue at the centre of a greater ecosystem.

It has been revealed that fenway Sports Group – born around the Boston Red Sox and Liverpool FC – have developed a holding manufacturer with interests in media, marketing, real estate, and entertainment. It’s a model Cardinale knows first hand: in 2021, RedBird invested approximately $750m in FSG, acquiring a stake of around 11%, based on an enterprise valuation of $7.35bn.

Industry observers note that MSE in theory can harness elements of all three of these experiences: KSE’s integration of sports and infrastructure, AEG ‘s commercial development of facilities and FSG ‘s multi-sport approach. The main difference is the purpose declared by Cardinale: to use all of it to funnel money back into Milan.

From the stadium shared with Inter to the possibility of an arena in San Donato, including the fresh NBA Europe venture and even tennis: MSE’s scope includes various initiatives that go beyond the playing field.

The main infrastructure project is the future Generali Stadium, the new 71,500-seat facility designed by Foster + Partners and Manica. Developed jointly by the two Milanese clubs, it represents a key element of the transformation of the San Siro area and will not be a Rossoneri-only facility.

The promoters intend for the stadium to host year-round activities, from matches to concerts, as well as catering, events, and hospitality services. In other words, like the stadiums and arenas mentioned above, it will become more than just a place to go for two hours on a Sunday.

In San Donato Milanese, RedBird are also considering the possibility of building a 20,000-seat arena. Cardinale explained that the fund already owns the land and has planning permission, but the idea is also linked to Milan’s potential involvement in NBA Europe. Another area of ​​focus concerns tennis, with the possibility of hosting a tournament in the city.

Recent findings suggest that finally, RedBird intend to develop a company dedicated to managing stadiums and arenas, with services including catering, merchandising and premium hospitality. The goal is to build commercial expertise to apply to the facilities connected to the group, but also to make it available to other owners and sports clubs.

Sources indicate that this phase will be co-ordinated by Brett Yormark, appointed CEO of MSE and set to step down as head of the Big 12 (a conference in College Football) at the end of January 2027. He worked for 14 years at Brooklyn Sports & Entertainment, overseeing the development of the Brooklyn Nets and the Barclays Center. He has also gained experience in NASCAR and Roc Nation.

The choice to go for Yormark reflects the desire to entrust the platform to someone with expertise across multiple different fields in the sporting and commercial worlds.

All these grand intends are well and good, but how will ideas turn into money that drives AC Milan forward? MSE’s economic potential is measured not only through the club’s revenues, but also through the activities that RedBird intends to develop around sports, infrastructure and entertainment.

Industry observers note that the starting point is obviously Milan as a club, which closed the 2025-26 financial year with revenues of €464.6m, over €100m of which came from sponsorships. The main infrastructure opportunity is the fresh San Siro, an investment of approximately €2.3bn shared with Inter.

Projections contained in the design documents indicate a potential annual revenue of approximately €120.4m for the facility as a whole (both for the Rossoneri and the Nerazzurri), through sporting, commercial, and complementary services.

Industry observers note that these are numbers that will be revised upwards by the two clubs when considering, for example, the record agreement with Generali for naming rights. It is worth a total of €650m over 25 years, divided into €10m per year for the first five years and €30m per season for the following 20, once the stadium is built.

It has been revealed that one of the areas on which RedBird Capital are focusing most is hospitality, which is currently worth around €15m per year for the Rossoneri. The international benchmark has already been set by Legends Global, a company Cardinale knows well.

Recent findings suggest that legends are what the Milan owner sees as a model for developing premium services, restaurants, and commercial spaces. The most obvious example is at FC Barcelona: with the support of LG, the club have marketed nearly 5,000 VIP seats at Camp Nou, generating over €380m in contracted revenue.

They aim to generate another €700m through multi-year licenses for an additional 2,000 seats. This isn’t annual revenue, but rather contracts spread over 15 or 30 years, so a guaranteed flow of money coming in that Cardinale aims to replicate.

Another agreement which demonstrates the potential of this kind of arrangement is the one with Real Madrid for the Santiago Bernabéu. It involves an investment of approximately €360m in exchange for 20-year participation in some of the stadium’s businesses,.

Legends Global also operate in facilities and events management. Following the acquisition of ASM Global (who actually proposed renovating San Siro for non-football events in Italy) in 2024, the group claims a presence in over 450 venues, approximately 20,000 events, and 165 million guests annually. Their European partnerships include Arsenal, Chelsea and Porto.

FC Barcelona introduces new VIP seating licenses at Spotify Camp Nou with Legends Global.

🔗 More details: https://t.co/awtEsnYE6X pic.twitter.com/iCMuM0QD35.

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) September 25, 2026.

To illustrate the potential it could hold for Italy as a whole, the English subsidiary reported revenues of £131.6m in 2024, of which £105.5m came from facility and event management and £26.1m from catering. Before the integration with ASM Global, Legends had reported revenues of $1.7bn in the period ending in March 2024, with 67% coming from food and beverage sales.

In Italy, a benchmark is Forumnet, who in 2024 generated €29.7m in revenue and €12.8m in EBITDA (Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation). They manage the Assago Forum which hosts approximately 60-70 concerts a year, demonstrating how a venue can generate activity well beyond the sports calendar.

As mentioned, an arena is being planned in San Donato with an estimated investment of around €400m, which could become the basis for a Milanese franchise in NBA Europe. For reference, Olimpia Milano – the current basketball team in the city – generate around €15m through ticketing, season tickets, sponsorships and merchandising.

It has been revealed that for NBA Europe, projections speak of over $1.5bn to be distributed to the clubs in the first six years. A theoretical division among the 12 permanent franchises would equate to approximately $20.8m per team per year, but this is not fixed yet. Entry costs – estimated by the media to be between $500m and over $1bn – also remain to be determined.

Tennis represents another potential area for development. The ATP 500 in Halle generates around €5m in revenue, excluding television rights, while the ATP Finals in Turin generate around €60m. These are events with different dimensions and scopes, but they provide a scale.

The creation of MSE has a stated objective: to strengthen Milan’s financial capacity and reduce the gap with the richest clubs on the international scene, particularly those in the Premier League.

In a recent development, the gap is also evident when comparing revenues. AC Milan closed the 2025-26 season with €464.6m, a significant result considering their absence from European competitions , but still far from the top English clubs.

According to recent reports, according to the Deloitte Football Money League, in the 2024-25 season, Liverpool generated €836.1m, Arsenal €821.7m and Manchester United €793.1m. Tottenham and Chelsea also exceeded €670m and €580m, respectively.

The comparison covers different financial years, but it still indicates the magnitude of the gap. Liverpool generated revenues equal to approximately 1.8 times those of Milan, while Chelsea recorded a turnover approximately €120 higher.

The chasm demonstrates how clubs in the Premier League have showcased an ability to generate commercial revenue, enhance stadiums and reach a global audience. The gap has only been growing, and TV rights will be another focus, though that is outside of just Cardinale’s hands.

It has been revealed that speaking of the owner, it is now obvious he sees MSE as the name that will house the tools to try build a real sporting and commercial world around Milan. It remains to be seen how effective it will be, but the starting point is there.

The Red Devils are desperate for cover at left-back with Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu both hampered by injury, and Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot, both natural right-backs, used in that position as deputies.

It is belived that the La Liga club are so desperate to let the defender leave - so they can free up space in their wage budget for new signings - that they could agree to a deal that would favour United considerably.

Pochettino takes charge of his first game in charge of United on Sunday, when they take on Liverpool at Anfield.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In the final Premier League match before the November international break, the Red Devils and Villans played out a 4-4 draw at Old Trafford.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 16:00.

The KMI Panel has unanimously claimed that Manchester United's decisive equaliser against Aston Villa was correctly awarded.

In the final Premier League match before the November international break, the Red Devils and Villans played out a 4-4 draw at Old Trafford.

Villa twice held two-goal advantages - at 2-0 and 4-2 - before United scored twice in added-on time to earn a deserved share of the spoils.

However, there were question marks over whether Patrick Dorgu's last-gasp equaliser should have stood.

United goalkeeper Senne Lammens, who had joined the attack for a corner, seemingly deliberately made contact with opposite number Zion Suzuki without making an attempt for the ball.

Despite it appearing clear that Lammens's only intention was to make contact with Suzuki, it has been deemed that the referee and VAR were correct not to award or advise a foul.

A five-person KMI Panel all determined that a foul had not been committed by Lammens, subsequently leading to VAR not being required to intervene.

The KMI Panel noted: "Although Lammens turned away from the ball, the contact he made on Suzuki was not impactful.".

Aston Villa chief Damian Vidagany took to social media in the day after the match to claim that all 20 Premier League clubs had been informed before the start of the season that such an action from any player would be penalised.

The incident was one which brought up a genuine debate over whether the goal should have stood, but the fact that the KMI Panel voted unanimously against a foul being committed could open a can of worms.

Managers and players will, logically, now attempt to replicate the level of interference from Lammens, aware that they could avoid punishment from officials.

Pochettino, who arrived at Carrington to begin work on Wednesday, will be tasked with guiding United away from the bottom three and as high up the top-flight table as he can, while also seeing how far he can get his fresh side in the Champions League.

The 54-year-old will be keen to stamp his authority on the playing squad at Old Trafford, particularly with a number of key players’ contracts expiring at the end of the current campaign.

Captain Fernandes turned down a second new contract offer last week to throw his future further into doubt, while question marks remain over the other three.

It is believed that United are eyeing reinforcements at centre-back, left-back and up front in the upcoming transfer window, with injuries hampering them across all three positions.

At left-back and centre-forward, they are particularly light after issues for Shaw, Patrick Dorgu and Benjamin Sesko.

Pochettino is expected to be consulted on any potential incomings at Old Trafford, and it is thought that the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will have significant input into who comes through the door.

‘I followed him at Bristol City, and when he was there, I was speaking to someone that knew him who told me he was a Tottenham fan.

Chelsea are reportedly leading the hotly contested race to sign Scott and are said to be increasingly confident of reaching an agreement with Bournemouth for the central midfielder.

However, Waddle insists Scott should ideally be aiming higher than a move to Stamford Bridge, name-checking Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal as potential options.

‘According to reports, Chelsea retain the strongest interest in him. No disrespect to them, but I think he can look higher. I think he’s got the ability to play for the biggest teams in Europe: Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich, PSG, Arsenal,’ he added.

‘The guy looks like he’s a top player to me. He looks like he’s only going to get better. If I was a manager or a sporting director and I needed a midfielder, I would be looking at him.

In a recent development, ‘He’s a complete midfielder. He can play as a 10, an 8, and a 6. He offers you a bit of everything. He reminds me a little bit of Rodri in the way that he likes to take the ball off the centre-back and start making things happen.

‘His composure and technique make him a standout player for any team looking to sign someone who can run a midfield and control the tempo.’.

While Bournemouth are in no hurry to part with Scott, the club’s hierarchy recognise that the England international may have ambitions to move on elsewhere near future.

For now, though, the Cherries are adamant that the Vitality Stadium remains the ‘right place’ for Scott.

‘At this point, we’re convinced that we’re the right place for Alex to be, for Alex to stay, and we’ll keep on addressing contract challenges with Alex as we move through this year,’ Bournemouth owner Bill Foley told talkSPORT last month.

‘We’d love to have Alex stay here, sign a new contract and be part of this team for the long haul, and we’re still working on it. We haven’t given up.

‘But sometimes players get stars in their eyes and they think that Chelsea is the right place to go or Manchester City.’.

Scott’s current contract on the south coast runs through to June 2028.

How measuring the state of nature can reverse biodiversity loss

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1847 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the world’s largest wildlife bridge is under construction in Agoura Hills, California, and will enable animals to cross US Route 101 safely.
  • Biodiversity is the cornerstone of human survival — providing us with food, shelter, medicines, clean air and water, and contributing to our general well-being.
  • To build a better world, stop chasing economic growth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the world’s largest wildlife bridge is under construction in Agoura Hills, California, and will enable animals to cross US Route 101 safely. Credit: Kevin Carter/Getty.

Biodiversity is the cornerstone of human survival — providing us with food, shelter, medicines, clean air and water, and contributing to our general well-being. Its continuing loss is a major risk to us and to the global economy.

To build a better world, stop chasing economic growth.

To build a better world, stop chasing economic growth.

Sources indicate that extreme degradation of ecosystems is projected to cost the world at least US$2.7 trillion, or 2.3% of global gross domestic product, each year by 20301. That’s almost three times more than the annual cost of protecting nature (up to $967 billion)2, a figure that happens to be similar to the amount governments paid in 2024 to subsidize the fossil-fuel industry ($920 billion; see go.nature.com/4ejtafn).

Sources indicate that those stark numbers should drive efforts to protect nature. In 2022, the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework set out an ambitious pathway to reach the vision of a world living in harmony with nature by 20503. But what’s missing is a way to measure progress. A systematic approach to tracking biodiversity losses and attempts to reverse them is urgently needed.

The Nature Positive Initiative (NPI) has begun to do this by developing metrics to record the ‘state of nature’. Launched in 2023, the NPI is a consortium of the world’s largest sustainable business and finance coalitions and conservation organizations.

Cities and countryside are intimately linked — green initiatives must recognize that.

Cities and countryside are intimately linked — green initiatives must recognize that.

In a recent development, the metrics aim to provide a globally consistent minimal framework — a simple common language — for tracking changes in nature across countries and sectors. They were developed through a consensus process and measure ecosystem extent and condition, species extinction risks and population trends across terrestrial, freshwater and marine realms4.

They are also designed to integrate with existing global standards and frameworks for reporting and disclosing nature-related financial risks, such as the Science Based Targets Network (SBTN)5 and the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD)6. This compatibility increases the likelihood that scientifically sound metrics will be reported and embedded by businesses and financial institutions in their disclosures and policies, and in systems for risk management and investment — all of which are essential to decision-making.

Industry observers note that so far, the metrics have been tested with 29 companies across 23 countries at more than 50 sites. However, they still need rigorous, independent assessment in real-world contexts to ascertain whether they are practical to implement and really improve environmental outcomes. Without empirical validation, there is a risk that these nature metrics might generate misleading signals to investors, fail to detect meaningful ecological change or impose monitoring cost burdens that limit the uptake of biodiversity projects.

Here we highlight four challenges and a way forward.

Industry observers note that although they are called metrics, the NPI measures are in fact a broad framework of indicators and recording approaches. Their focus on assessing the broad ‘state’ of ecosystems, rather than concentrating on the pressures on nature or actions for protection, is an important shift. It moves companies away from simply reporting their activities, instead making them and others accountable for outcomes. But it leaves latitude in how organizations will interpret and apply the metrics, potentially weakening their overall impact.

Industry observers note that for example, the metrics have three levels of detail or precision — preparatory, medium and high — to recognize the uneven global distribution of data, expertise and resources. Although this flexibility makes them easier to apply in diverse settings, it creates challenges for comparability and interpretation when assessments are undertaken on different spatial scales or levels of precision.

The Tiaozini wetlands in eastern China are a crucial ecological hub.Credit: Costfoto/NurPhoto via Getty.

The idea is that companies will get on board early with the preparatory level of precision and then progress towards more high-quality, ecologically meaningful measures and outcomes. A preparatory-level assessment might use data with relatively coarse spatial resolution and classify land cover as natural or not natural, for instance. More-advanced assessments would have higher resolution and use more-precise ecosystem classifications.

The concern is that organizations might cherry-pick ‘easy’ ecosystem characteristics or species to measure, potentially biasing their reporting towards apparent gains rather than describing those that are meaningful. For instance, common species are more likely to respond well to ecological improvements than specialist species are, even though the specialists might be a higher priority for conservation.

Over-reporting of improvements, particularly in relation to ecosystem connectivity and extent, can provide a misleading sense of how well species can survive genetic and demographic challenges. Better understanding of these measures is also key in guarding against changes that might not only bring benefits but also could do harm, such as when connectivity promotes the movement of invasive species that alter the local ecosystem.

In a recent development, another challenge is that nature is forever changing through a myriad of interactions between living species and the environment, as well as with shifting global processes such as climate change. With simple metrics, there is a risk that complex, dynamic processes and non-linear changes will be missed and the damages and risks underestimated.

How biodiversity credits could help to conserve and restore nature.

How biodiversity credits could help to conserve and restore nature.

Measuring the number of hectares restored, for instance, can indicate where conservation action has occurred, but not whether nature has recovered, ecosystem functions have been reinstated or threatened species populations are increasing.

It has been revealed that the inclusion of ecosystem condition and species status measures in the NPI metrics aim to address this complexity. But this will work only if they are not simplified to the point at which they no longer provide an accurate and comprehensive assessment of how a site is changing.

According to recent reports, reconciling the tension between a global approach for nature impacts and the local ecological and sociopolitical experiences of these impacts is challenging. Although global consistency is essential for corporate reporting so that investors can make informed comparisons, at the local level, biodiversity protection and the financial impacts and dependencies of communities on natural resources are inherently context-specific. Metrics designed to support global comparisons between organizations might overlook ecological, cultural and social values that are notable locally.

Why environmental treaties must also address mental health.

Why environmental treaties must also address mental health.

Many owners of the state of nature metrics and global biodiversity frameworks will draw heavily on global data sets. Such resources include the Global Forest Watch Open Data Portal and the Copernicus Global Dynamic Land Cover product for ecosystem extent and condition, and the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species as a proxy for species that are at risk of extinction.

Industry observers note that but without on-the-ground verification, the metrics will fail, particularly in data-poor regions, by misrepresenting fine-scale ecological conditions and changes. Relying on remote-sensing products that describe only the tree canopy, for example, can miss much about the structure of the forest below. Indigenous knowledges might also be disregarded. Overlooking local values and knowledge is concerning because it reinforces the broader global pattern of marginalizing local communities in environmental decision-making.

Implementation of the metrics and the incentives behind them that push companies to engage with nature measurement are likely to have both positive and negative impacts on nature and communities. What these impacts look like is currently unknown. This is why the metrics need to be independently tested to assess their value for nature, businesses and communities.

It has been revealed that impacts on nature will be driven by how priority species are determined, how the metrics are combined and compared and the time frame in which changes will be measured. For example, should equal weight be given to population change in critically endangered species and to species of important cultural value to local communities?

And how should owners compare shifts in the components of an ecosystem that typically change over decades (such as growth of a forest) to those that develop much more rapidly (such as the life cycles of pollinating insects)? Developing guidance on how to grapple with these complexities will be essential if the metrics are to describe the state of nature.
